title: Expected more
review: Just didn't live up to its hype. The movie is dull, with no straight line scenario. And this is by far the most important thing in this suspense/riddle kind of movie. Prometheus looks beautiful, making a step further in aspect of visual effects, but the cohesive force and atmosphere lacks. The movie is like a combination of 5 different scenarios and neither one made the goal.This movie ends with questions opened, but not in Inception way- where you can interpret end in a way that you like. In Prometheus you don't have enough information, since everything is explained briefly, and that is the biggest problem. All in all: not the worst ride, but definitively could have been groundbreaking. It is just mediocre, not more not less, with idea of being philosophical but falling too short.

title: Thought Provoking
review: If you are going to see Prometheus in the hope of seeing an "Alien" type movie then this is not the movie for you. This is not a monster movie. This is however an extremely thought provoking movie. The kind that you feel you probably have to watch two or three times before you can begin to understand it all. The characters were not the best or most original but they weren't unbearable either. Ridley Scott's style of filming definitely shows in this movie, being a very relaxed pace for the most part and not trying to rush any scenes along. This movie will make you scratch your head for sure the second it's over. And I thought Matrix was a complex movie!

title: Alright/good Sci-Fi/horror movie
review: Ridley Scotts' Latest Film 'Prometheus' is not that bad of a movie unlike the reviews you read here. If you were expecting a purely Scifi alone movie you should have known that Scott adds that twist of horror onto it to make it even better. I wont spoil too much to it but I will say it is worthwhile movie to watch there were several points in the movie that really stood out for me and even made me jump in my seat (From scared) and one where my heart was pounding. Few movies do that to me and I've been a sci-fi guy for a while and I'd have to give this movie an 8/10 for reasons there were some plots holes throughout the movie that maybe were mentioned/talked about but kinda glanced over. Sure there were some things/mistakes made but there isn't a movie that doesn't have plot holes your talking about trying to portray an idea/thoughts into a 2-3 hour time slot so your bound to make mistakes. Don't let the negative reviews get to you if you are looking to go see it go see it, in fact I'd be willing to see it again if i had another chance.

title: Really Enjoyable 2 Hours
review:
I have just returned from the Theater. Being a fan of the Alien series, I wanted to see this movie since it was first announced. I had read some negative reviews and some positive ones, but I went into the movie not to critique and try to line up Alien to this movie, but to just relax and enjoy. I was not disappointed. The story was great, I got to see scenes that made me say, oh yeah that is later seen in Alien, and I was surprised by the different plot choices. Many things you can see coming from a mile away, and some of the choices made were stupid, but it did not follow the cookie cutter routine. Never did one person go off alone, the person in charge did not make calls that were utterly unbelievable (I still hate the call in alien to let the infected guy on board despite regulations.)

The only reason I drop two stars is that it is becoming like Lost. We are given questions, but never answers. Why did the Engineer start killing everyone. Why did the Engineers stockpile the black ooze, What occurs that changes the planet to what we see in Alien? These are questions that I hope Ridley Scott answers in the Sequel to this movie and prequel to Alien. Other than the lost type plot, I think this is worth seeing.

title: Are all prequels to franchise films fundamentally doomed?
review:
Prequels to films with fully-detailed ecosystems can play out like a grocery list of payoffs and 'tribute' scenes. Prometheus has that challenge. Sir Ridley Scott came from the world of commercials where the stereotypes must reveal/explain and play themselves out quickly. So we have all the Alien "hooks" in place and plenty of sci fi genre hooks (Star Trek, Star Wars, Indiana Jones) all blended into a script that sometimes -- because of these hooks -- distracts rather than enthralls.

Yes, there has to be a corporate expedition, and a diverse crew and crew conflicts and an amoral robot and slimy creatures. Check, check and check. But where is the growing sense of dread that worked so well in Alien? Granted, this is -- by necessity -- derivative stuff. But I watched Prometheus from a distance. Never with the sense of intimate menace that Alien so brilliantly exploited.

There is one situation that is so preposterous and distracting that it took me right out of the film -- and I was barely in it, anyway. The best science fiction puts you into the world you are observing and uses that to give you new perspectives. Prometheus was at times a bit like a thing wriggling in a test tube. Fascinating, but safely removed and not really threatening.

Did I dislike the film? I did not. I rated it a 6/10. It sustained my interest. It simply didn't thrill me. By all means, see it. However, do not go in with high expectations.

title: Prometheus lands in the wrong place...
review:
God, I was waiting so much for this film and that feeling was finally satiated. After Scott's classic sci-fi Alien, here comes a prequel that provides answers to some questions that were raised in the 1979 classic. This film gets a mixed review. Some say it's poor story but great visuals. Some say it's Scott's best and it has great visuals. Some say it was thrilling yet boring still visuals were great. My opinion is somewhat mixed... Don't worry, there are no spoilers here.

What is Prometheus? Wikipedia says: "Prometheus is a Titan, culture hero, and trickster figure who in Greek mythology is credited with the creation of man from clay and the theft of fire for human use, an act that enabled progress and civilization. He is known for his intelligence, and as a champion of mankind." In the film, scientists Elizabeth Shaw (Noomi Rapace) and Charlie Holloway (Logan Marshall- Green) discover clues on Earth that leads them to a half a billion away solar system where the "Engineers" of mankind themselves probably reside. The ship that takes them there is named Prometheus. It's a two year journey so the 16 crew members are kept in hibernation, guarded by an Android named David (Michael Fassbender). After they land, they discover extremely weird stuff which I won't reveal. What happens next is the search for answers, the truth, the truth about our creators which believe me really isn't so much satisfying.

Yep, everyone agrees that the film looks powerfully stunning thanks to the jaw-dropping visual effects equipped with a stunning cinematography and of course 3D. The film begins with a beautiful view of our Earth's geology but minus life. Here we see how we were engineered, how it all began. Another stunning element that adds up to the film is the ingenious electronic score. It's completely perfect for the experience. The sound design, being another important element in any sci-fi film, gets a perfect score from me. All in all, Ridley Scott's Prometheus deserves a standing ovation for the beautiful world that he has very realistically and smartly created just the way Alien and Blade Runner was.

Okay, now have a seat. Stunning visuals aren't going to save the film because instead of solving the questions (which it does) more questions arise like who created our Engineers? And the biggest one is: What happens next, dude? As many people said, the film has flaws. Yes, there are but I guess what they most probably meant by that was "This is another clichéd sci-fi that was not expected from a Director like Scott". I guess they are right. Like for example the whole crew. Now there are 17 of them. When the film enters it's intense last hour, it looks like they were simply lining up for slaughter, getting killed one by one. It sort of felt like they were expendable or something. Scott really treats them that way and the film kind of makes special arrangements for the key characters. In another scene, a character has a quick abdominal surgery to remove the Alien fetus. Surprisingly, with the stapled cut, she walks and joins the intensity of the film again in no time. I believe that most people were disappointed just because they were comparing it to Alien. Prometheus doesn't have a subtle style, a rich story, it seriously forgets common sense in some scenarios, etc. There are far too many flaws to overlook. You feel like "Hey what was the point of all those intense emotional and thrilling moments if you yourself don't see the point?"

I guess you will enjoy Prometheus a little more if you stop comparing it to the almost-perfect-thriller Alien. It's a Prequel, so treat it as one. The flaws did disappoint me, really unexpected from a director like Ridley Scott. More blame goes to the poor screenplay. But I think movies are sometimes made just for monetary purposes, not for serious art or to satisfy a die-hard fan's nostalgia. Prometheus is one of them. Come on, film-making is a business too right? I will still forgive and forget the flaws and say that it was overall a marvelous experience. I still believe Scott is a brilliant movie-maker. Prometheus is a good start to the series and the film, judging by the conclusion, promises another adventure which I doubt won't be possible.

As for the performances, Sweden's "Girl with the Dragon tattoo" Noomi Rapace has the same strong femininity that Weaver showed in Alien. I have always been strangely attracted to these kind of women in movies who show great survival instincts without forgetting their emotions. Fassbender is the best thing about Prometheus, very powerful in his performance of the Android David. These two were the best in the entire ensemble.

In conclusion, there are flaws and some moments will leave you scratching your head. Yes, it isn't one of Scott's best but I don't think it's worst either. For now, just enjoy and try to take in all the "entertaining" stuff that this film very ingeniously provides as it's not only mysterious but also freaking scary at times!

So now one excitement ends, another begins. Pixar's Brave is releasing on 22nd so stay tuned. This year we are really anticipating a lot of good movies, I just hope none of them lets us down. Have a nice Day and take care. Hope you enjoy this film nevertheless. Thanks for reading.

title: It's Alien, Jim but not as we know it.
review: Ridley Scott's Alien-prequel is like a Christmas present sitting under a tree. Attractively wrapped it promises to be the present you always wanted. But come Christmas morning as you begin to unwrap it, it quickly dawns on you that you haven't received the Playstation 3 you always wanted. Sure the box says it's a Playstation but once you open it, it turns out it's another knitted jumper from Grandma. As any fan of Alien will tell you, Prometheus concerns the large humanoid, or "Space Jockey" seen at the beginning of that film. Ever since that memorable scene fans have wondered what it was and why it was there. Well, after watching Prometheus they're still wondering. This film probably sounded better when the producers discussed it around the production table. Sadly the end result simply doesn't work. There are too many needless characters, too much bad dialogue and not nearly enough thrills or suspense that Alien and Aliens gave us in spades. Poorly written, this mishmash of ideas turns out to be a sheep in wolf's clothing. The premise (I hesitate to use the word plot as there isn't really one) concerns an expedition to a faraway world to discover the possible origins of mankind. When our explorers reach the planet of LV-223 (not LV-426 featured in Alien and revisited in Aliens) they discover several large structures in a barren wasteland. It soon becomes apparent that the giant humanoids were our ancestors (surprise surprise) and the large structures are in fact alien vessels - the doughnut shaped ship from Alien being one of them. Our intrepid explorers find out they these humanoids were wiped out by some kind of biological weapon that they created and wished to destroy the Earth with. Soon things go down the tubes and, just like in Alien, there is only one female survivor. Why the giant humanoids were planning our destruction is not explained - though we can speculate, nor is the nature of the biological weapon, which appears to be a forerunner of the alien creature. In fact several things are not explained at all and all this does is leave you with a sense of disappointment. In fact it's no better or worse than the laughable Alien v Predator films. Michael Fassbender is amusing as an effeminate robot and Charlize Theron looks smoking hot as the ice-cool corporate suit from Weyland Industres. You'd be better of watching Stargate.

title: A thought-provoking premise falls short.
review:
I wanted to love this movie. The cinematography, scope, and concept evoke awe. The execution was at times flawed, but nearing the end of the film, I was happy I had come.

Without giving too much away, when we all think the movie is over, the director gives us all a little extra. Unfortunately, this "little extra" ends up feeling gratuitous, manufactured, and banal.

Ultimately, the movie fails in its vain attempt to be both a prequel and a movie in its own right. The sheer beauty of the cinematography and the computer graphics is staggering. The acting was thoroughly believable. Clearly borrowing from better films, such as Star Wars, Alien, The Fifth Element, and Star Trek, it nearly achieved such greatness but for an inability to take its audience seriously enough to go beyond the profit-driven motive to set up a sequel and end the movie with integrity.

It will leave you unsatisfied.

5/10

title: Knee jerkers need to give their head a shake
review:
I don't usually feel the need to review titles but the level of 1,2 & 3 star reviews of this movie has motivated me to write.

I also wouldn't usually feel the need to throw down credentials but i'm not a fat popcorn eating simpleton, I'm portly and prefer a 3 scoop sundae who majored in film & media.

First thing i have to say is that this movie is visually jaw dropping from the first scene and never lets up on that front. The universe that Scott has created was immersive and made me wish I'd opted for the IMAX experience rather than 2D.

Now for the main reason I'm writing this. Some of the aspects of this film being used to justify poor reviews.

Unrealistic: The abortion scene has been used as an example of extreme stupidity. How can she have stomach surgery and manage to be fine afterwards? Your absolutely correct, it makes no sense, and if i were watching a medical drama set in the present day I'd be right with you. In reality your watching a Sci Fi movie, i tend to suspend my disbelief in this scenario and just go with it. It's part of the joy of the genre for me. Look what they can do in the future, how cool is that! In addition the scene works from a cinematic POV. People around me were wincing in there seats.

Poor character development: I can't agree with this either. I thought Fassbenders character was brilliantly Machiavellian and beautifully acted. I thought he'd set a high bench mark in Shame but this performance sends him into another league for me.

Rapace is immense too, her character is well formed and really manages to drive the plot. I don't disagree that some of the dialogue is a little clunky at times but again, show me a sci fi movie where there are no moments like that. I can't think of many.

The other characters are under developed but what do you want? They don't have the benefits of being a 12 part TV series or episode 3 of a 6 part franchise. They are there for one purpose, to drive the plot and they serve their purpose. There are 17 members of the ship and i personally couldn't be bothered having to sit through hours of character development in a movie theatre. I think it would have slowed down the plot.

I agree whole heartedly with the Guy Pearce issue, why not just get an old fella in to play the part? He looked a bit silly and added nothing to the role.

The whole film occurs in the Alien universe but is a distant prequel to the Alien movie, this again buys the movie a lot of credit. The questions it raises aren't meant to be answered in this movie. It's plainly leaving room to manoeuvre in future films and I'm not going to leave my thoughts on what things meant or where thing are going from here.

I gave the film a 7/10 as it's not without flaws, for what it's worth Alien and Blade Runner for me are 8/10 movies. Scott has managed to create another fantastic world with a compelling story that adds to the Alien universe. If you can check your baggage at the door and do the reasonable thing, suspend your disbelief, your in for a cinematic treat. If you go in wanting it to be Alien mark 2 be prepared to be disappointed.

title: No more anti-prequels please.
review:
Warning - this post contains anti-spoilers from a better version of a Prometheus movie.

Come on! For 200 million, you couldn't throw us a bone? Since 1979, we've all been waiting to find out where the aliens came from and how smart they are. Neither one was even hinted at in a deserving way. Even the fake spoiler script online was better.

How hard would it have been to get a bunch of Alien fans together to find out what they wanted to see?

Even Giler and Hill were on this one. It looks like they went back to all their original Alien drawings before they hired Giger and decided the BAD ideas from the first movie would pass for an anti-prequel.

To prove my point, read my version of an Alien prequel below. It took me fifteen minutes to come up with this and I work for a living.

1. A combination of prospectors, colonists, robots, and hired guns head out from Earth 100 years before the first Alien film. They arrive at their destination, an Earth-like planet they were expecting to be free of intelligent life. They discover that the entire population was humanoid and wiped out by an unknown force.

2. Before landing, they scan the planet and find a large dome structure still radiating energy. They land in desperation near the structure and decide to explore it. The crew discovers the planet's inhabitants were human and attacked by another race. Unknown to them, all around the planet, they find petrified alien eggs.

3. They can't get into the interior of the dome but they discover the source of the energy and accidentally activate it. As they leave, a sleep chamber opens with the engineer race inside the dome.

4. The engineers awake and approach the human ship and want to meet them. The engineers describe the race wiped out as the aggressor and they were defending themselves. They are very anxious to know where Earth is and any other human planets are. The humans are suspicious and decide to infiltrate their dome to get answers.

5. In the dome, the humans discover the engineers released the aliens and wiped out the planet they are on. The robot crew members are able to decode information in the dome and discover the alien takes the biological form of the attacked race and dies out when the attackers arrive. It's also able to pass genetic memory on from the host to the adult alien and queen.

6. Engineers try to take over the human ship with force and the use of the xenomorph. The humans fight back. There's a lot of running around, alien attacks, and more information is discovered. The Engineers created man as a slave race to do all the work once the Engineers arrived on a planet. Man became too smart too fast and started fighting back when they would arrive. They created the alien to wipe man out and start over.

7. After more running around and alien attacks, the Engineers discover where Earth is. The remaining Engineers take one of their other ships filled with alien eggs and head for Earth. The final heroine is infected with an alien but is able to get on the Engineer's ship. She fights back and takes control of the ship by getting in the "navigator-jockey" suit. In the end, she crash lands on a remote isolated moon just as the alien inside her bursts through the control suit. She sets off the warning beacon and dies.

title: In space, nobody can hear you yawn.
review:
I really wanted to love this movie. I love most of what Ridley's done over the years. And I usually don't write reviews, so forgive me my sophomoric style. But I have something I am compelled to say about this particular movie.

Prometheus has some fantastic elements, some very thoughtful, some funny, and some frightening. It has great CGI, beautiful ships, cool sets, Charlize-freaking-Theron.. all of which are potentially the soup of a great movie. And I can forgive holes in scripts, or ambiguous endings or threads of sub-story endings...

But where this movie fails is in the glue that holds it all together. The main storyline fails at grabbing all these disparate pieces, fitting them into a seamless (or even spotty) whole, and lifting them (and us in the process) up to a new level at the climax of the film. So ultimately, any of the elements of Prometheus, including Charlize-Freaking-Theron (whom I adore, if you didn't notice), become dispensable. They seem detached, and unimportant.

So what exactly is the storyline anyway?

I think it's actually about hubris - Ridley Scott's hubris in thinking he could take all of these multi-million dollar elements, put them in a blender with Charlize-Freaking-Theron and Naomi Rapace, and leave it to the viewers to make Promethean apologetics that would form an actual main storyline in the process. It was hubris believing we would ultimately envisage an underlying genius, given enough time.

I believe the old man in this film is symbolic of Ridley Scott. He has the money and the power to form this voyage, but really has no idea what is waiting at the end. Rather than sharing his wisdom and telling us what he does know, he will squander his chances by having his own creation attempt to interpret it for him of its own volition. Which will of course lead to mayhem and *** SPOILER ALERT*** ...more headless robots.

I think giving it six out of ten stars is generous.

title: A great revival to the franchise
review:
Prometheus is the first original movie I have been excited for in a long time, and with Ridley Scott at the helm I knew it wouldn't disappoint.

Firstly, the visuals and cinematography were beautifully done and coordinated. The special effects were used to display the script and not the knowledge of the visual team, like many other movies rely on today. The music also completed each scene with necessary suspense and flowed perfectly throughout the film.

There were not many, if any, slow parts in the movie. I was either on the edge of my seat anticipating an alien encounter, being drawn in by the elaborate alien planet, or acknowledging the amazing acting by the cast.

Michael Fassbender portrayed David in such detail at times I forgot he was human and not the android he was portraying. Noomi Rapace livened up the screen with her curiosity, passion, and fear with an exceptional performance. The supporting cast of veterans (Charlize Theron and Idris Elba) added typical A class performances, while relative newcomer Logan Marshall-Green performed above my expectations and fit well in his part.

What I would have liked to see more of was more development of Charlize Theron, Idris Elba, and some of the supporting cast. I feel their performances could have been elevated even higher if they had just a little more background.

Overall Prometheus was a perfect start to bring back the Alien franchise. If it had been cut to a PG-13 rating many of the critical scenes would have been lost and the movie would not have the same terrifying stomach bursting terror that was brought to the big screen thirty years ago. Noomi Rapace made the movie shine bright with her performance as she led the all star cast to a movie masterpiece.

title: Brings back the tension of the first Alien movie
review:
I am a huge fan of 'Alien'. The slow burn, and the build-up of tension really heightened the horror atmosphere of that first film. And having been disappointed by subsequent films (though I still enjoyed all of them, except for the awful AvP craziness), I found it a wonderful surprise that Ridley Scott managed to bring that same feel back with 'Prometheus'.

Well, similar at least. 'Alien' was very dark and exuded hopelessness at every turn. 'Prometheus' has that same build up and tension, but visually it's brighter, and even thematically it's sprinkled with themes of faith and hope, which drives some of the major characters. Until they die horrible deaths at least.

I won't pretend to be an expert on 'Alien' mythology and lore so I can't really comment on how faithful it is to the Wikipedia articles or the comics or whatnot, but this movie sure answered a lot of questions for me, and raised a few of its own (which will probably be answered in the inevitable sequel).

And, well...let's just say that the story seems to be moving forward, in a more mature sci-fi style, and I find it an exhilarating and good kick in the pants for the franchise.

title: "Prometheus" Provides Little Satisfaction as a Pointless Prequel to "Alien"
review:
Walking out of the press screening for "Prometheus" I couldn't help thinking to myself, "This is what I've been waiting almost four years for?" I filled out my questionnaire, gave it to the Fox representative, and walked away telling my fellow movie reviewers goodbye. I stated that I hoped I could have a better day after it started out being ruined by a morning filled with disappointment delivered by Ridley Scott. I could sum up my review of the film in one sentence: Lower your expectations.

"Prometheus" felt tired to me. It was a conglomeration of recycled ideas and nostalgic bits and pieces spread out so "Alien" fanboys and girls could look over at each other and wink while watching it together. Fanatics of the franchise will be "in on" the subtle and not-so subtle references to the original, while others who never saw it won't be "lost." That being said, the only viewers who should be surprised by anything that happens in this movie are those who never experienced "Alien."

"Alien" enthusiasts need to see "Prometheus." Although it's pointless and disappointing in the grand scheme of things, it was mildly interesting to see the events talked about in the original film played out in front of me. Just don't go into it expecting for the film to break new ground or terrify you the way "Alien" did in 1979.

title: Ultra Spoilers
review: Prometheus works to hard at setting up a sequel to the prequel and as such it disrupts the story being told. So when the new explorers search another world to find the secrets of origination of man and the dying of old age funder is on a personal quest for 'please save me alien masters', they instead come across an alien biological experiment (humanity) clean up program. The hidden story here, the sequel to the prequel, is the Alien Engineers are obviously not happy with humans being used as prey by the Predator Aliens and as part of the breeding program of Reptilian Aliens (for want of a better description to prevent confusion between three sets of aliens). So using the Reptilian Alien DNA, the Engineer Aliens develop a biological weapon to eliminate the human species the Engineer Aliens originally created and remove them from the Alien Reptilian breeding cycle, assuming a conflict between the Engineer Aliens and the Predator Aliens and the Reptilian Aliens. The biological weapon gets out of control disrupting the Engineer Alien plot to eliminate humanity. When the human explorers arrive and start playing horny goof balls in space, they set up the scenario for Engineer Alien biological weapon to revert to type after gestation within a human and consequently a new chest burster in the surviving Engineer Alien. So ultra spoiler you can guess what the rest of the sequel to the prequel is all about, surviving human takes off to find out all about the Engineer Alien, Predator Alien, and Reptilian Alien conflict and humans the Engineers Aliens creation being used to breed up more Reptilian Aliens. Catch is, the build up to ensure a sequel to the prequel overloads the prequel so much it will likely kill of any chance of a sequel and having the rest of the story told.

title: Entertaining enough but not destined to become a classic
review:
Let me first say that I enjoyed this film, it had all the right tick boxes for me.

1. Genre. I love science fiction.

2. SFX, really good spaceships.

3. A robot that wants to be Peter O'Toole, really, he does.

4. A strong female lead character.

5. The film passes the Bechdel Test,but only just.

Now for the things that didn't quite work for me.

Some of the characters seemed to be very one dimensional, in fact several of them seemed quite pointless as they played no real part in the story. For example Vickers, ostensibly she is on the ship as a representative of the Weyland Corporation; however she is curiously separate from the rest of the crew. She has no function either on the ship or on the mission to investigate the alien planet. When she does give an order she is totally ignored . I can't help but think that someone somewhere thought that the cast needed a hot blonde.

Which brings us to two of the scientists who, having signed on for the exploration and subjected themselves to two years in cryosleep, then spend the entire time bitching about it while on board. And, when they finally get onto the planet they quickly become scared and want to rush back to the ship. Who screened these people before hiring them? The geologist Fifield, wanted to take a weapon onto the planet, I thought okay, he must be a security guard with the expedition party, but he turned out to be a geologist, but he took no tools of his trade with him, not even one teeny little rock hammer. Once there, he took one look at the dead alien, and promptly decided that that there was nothing on the planet for a geologist to investigate and headed back to the ship. It was a planet for God's sake; he was surrounded by alien rocks!! His sidekick, I'm still not entirely sure what sort of scientist he was decided to tag along. You might just as well have made them carry signs saying 'Dead Meat' or even just gone the whole hog and put them in red shirts!

The ship's pilots were there in order to die heroically, that's all. I don't think that we even learned their names.

But the main problem I have is, why would aliens go to the trouble of creating humans, leave us maps to the planet in the archaeological record, only to try to destroy us once we get there? And why would they want to infect Earth and get rid of us completely. Were we a failed experiment, or are the aliens playing with us and getting bored with their toys?

I will definitely go and see the next instalment, if only for an answer to that last question, but I'm not really expecting to be completely blown away as I was with the sequel to Alien.

title: Wants to be clever but isn't clever enough. - SPOILERS -
review:
There were obviously 2 ways to go, a clever 'origin of species' with a few nasty surprises, or a bug hunt. Scott chose the later despite, I suspect, most of the audience wanting more of an 'Aliens' type film (there really has only been one 'bug hunt' film). Well, that's fine, I'm reasonably intelligent, so was happy to get on board Prometheus and see what happens.

Hm. Well, do we take it that human kind was created by mistake, a strand of DNA not being destroyed by magic potion? Perhaps. So, they've realised their mistake and have decided to do away with us with an hugely unnecessarily elaborate mutagenic killing machine, creating in the process a fantastically hostile planet (earth) full of very nasty things indeed. Maybe. Whatever their reason, that is their purpose, it seems.

Right. So give us some kind of meaning. And, while you're about it, can you please provide some kind of explanation as to how the ship stumbled across a launching pad for all those innumerous ships. And how those paintings managed to identify their solar system, despite it seeming to be the case that the Engineers left before their creation. And how the nasty soon-to-become-Aliens managed to escape at the same time at each of the launching pods, derailing all of their efforts? And of all the ways of getting rid of human kind, why choose such a dangerous one? And why wait so long? And why did the crewman go mental having been sprayed with acid? How was he able to breathe in that atmosphere?

Now, I see what he was trying to do, and I know this board is littered with people who will blindly follow this film and not accept criticism of it, but that, sadly, is their problem. It was just disappointing.

Oh, and who is to say that Vickers wasn't a robot?

title: Big things, have small beginnings
review:
Let me start this review by stating that i absolutely loved Prometheus. I feel absolutely mesmerized by all the negative reviews this movie has been getting. Prometheus began as being a prequel to the movie Alien, by the same director (Ridley Scott), but was later changed to a spin off.

Now, Alien is probably my favorite movie ever. With that in mind, does this movie live up to the hype? Absolutely not. But, can this movie stand by itself as an enjoyable, thrilling, sci fi adventure? YES! Yes it can.

Here are some of the positives that this movie presents: stunning visuals, a great mood and atmosphere, an interesting cast (Fassbender and Theron are both amazing in this movie), an amazing soundtrack and some pretty disturbing moments.

Some people are complaining about one dimensional characters, which i didn't really notice. Apart from the minor characters, everyone appears to have a motivation in this movie.

Please, ignore the one star and two star ratings this movie has been getting. It does not deserve in any way that score. Keep in mind, this is not Alien, and you will not be disappointed. And if you have some doubts about your feelings, maybe watch it twice or more. This movie will get better with repeated viewings.

title: Visually stunning sci-fi from the master, Ridley Scott...
review: After having sometime to absorb Prometheus, I just wanted to share my thoughts of the movie without giving away too much. I loved the film, as usual Ridley Scott sets a benchmark for capturing the audience with his visual effects. Those expecting another mindless alien versus predator movie please stay away from this film...the acting and storytelling is too complex for your patience on this one. The story was fascinating in itself, and Ridley takes us on a journey across the universe as only he could do. Noomi and Charlize were amazing in this film. The music score was a bit disappointing, it sounded too much like a score set for the avengers part 2. It needed a much more darker tone such as the score Jerry Goldsmith did for the original Alien Film. The new score adapted some great classical pieces which fit in nicely. I have many questions on some key parts of the film which I think could be answered after I watch it again. My advice is to manage your expectations. Go into this film with an open mind and not preset only to see a movie about the 'Alien'. I feel Ridley wanted to take his storytelling in an entirely new direction and he suceeded where many others have failed. But then again that's why he is one of the greatest directors of all time. Of course the film will draw criticism for what it isn't...another Alien versus the helpless crew or group of gun toting marines movie. But haven't we been there and done that many times before?

title: What It Lacks in Plot, It Compensates in Suspense and Philosophical Depth
review:
It would be hard to compare this to Scott's introduction of the Alien species, but if I have to, I would say it lacks the kind of horror that Alien brought and its suspense falls flat, though not by much.

What it manages to do more than the first installment is that it adds a layer of philosophical, constantly in pursuit of the origins of mankind, and ultimately mortality. The visuals no doubt outmatched the original, thanks to modern technology, but the effects seem to be behind similarly foreign planets settings like Avatar.

The suspense is maintained since the arrival at the planet of our makers, and most would expect countless answers flooding in as the plot unfolds. That is not really the case. In fact, there are questions left unanswered. One thing is for sure, it is an enjoyment, though not the same kind when you are watching the original, and it seems to promise a sequel, which I will gladly watch should it come.

title: The film will be coming back to eat it's insides over and over again...
review:
I declare myself an Alien/Giger fan and probably know a bit too much about the universe of these creatures for my own good, but said that I am quite open to new ideas and reboots since this will always happen as long as film is business...

The film as a whole did not quite meet the expectations and could possibly be one of Ridley's downfalls.

Prometheus opens with beautiful photography and a very nice and subtle score (although the old one almost did not have one) that helps build the anticipation, but it is in this very scene where Ridley's initial rule of "not showing the foe until the end" was broken with a front shot of the space jockey with out it's helmet. If it was meant to be a film of discovery it certainly was not true to this idea.

The premise of the film was interesting and could have gone various ways but with a sloppy dialogue, useless scenes and senseless character reactions and arcs it made the whole thing collapse. Noomi Rapace is a great lead, Chalize Theron was practically useless and the whole Weyland ordeal coming into the 3rd act also was. David had to be the stand out of the film, keeps you on edge and his character was very intriguing since it was quite hard to read his real intentions. The film was very familiar and nothing new came out from it and when coming from Ridley Scott, the main pillar of Sci Fi, you expect it to be "different", instead he delivers something so close to Alien 3 and 4 that it's disappointing, specially when the peak of the film (Elizabeth Shaw trapped inside the medical capsule with the Alien) at the end of the 2nd Act is better than the finale.

But not all was bad, what kept me in my seat was the design and photography; although it did not look anything like Alien, I still enjoyed watching it. To be a film that had big expectations it was not big at all, just another way of filling up the pockets of producers and directors with a franchise that has been bled to death. The only reason is that I am giving this one a 7/10 is because I am intrigued with the next films to come, maybe the real film we are all expecting is coming our way...hopefully.

I still enjoyed it and would not stop anyone from watching this film, but beware, by no means sit through the film waiting for it to be like the classic; watch it as a stand alone film, that could possibly be forgotten.

title: --- May contain spoilers! ---
review:
"The perfect combination of a thriller, horror and sci-fi movie" is what comes to mind, after watching this movie. What didn't surprise me, after watching the movie, was all the bad reviews on IMDb. With all due respect, if you are a huge Alien 1,2,3 fan, you will be utterly disappointed by this movie. It seems that people who aren't really into the Alien films were amazed by this movie, while the Alien fans, in particular, were very disappointed and gave this movie low ratings, like 4/10, despite its great plot.

Personally, I am not extremely into the Alien series, although I think they are quite good. For this reason, I chose to not focus on the story enveloping the Alien films, and rather focus on the aspects of the movie.

To begin with, I loved the scenery in this movie, and some of the shots shade some directors completely. The shots of the waterfall, the planet, the inside of the ship, and the ruins on the planet are shot and displayed in a very great way, and for this we have to respect Ridley Scott. Most of the reviews managed to add how Ridley has "forgotten most there is to know about movies", but I disagree. He's still talented, and Prometheus was some incredible work, from his part.

The scenes in the beginning, where David is walking around on the ship, learning more about human technology, science and history is really good. I loved how they toned down that he was also studying the alien language. This gives us some sense of feeling that something mysterious is down on that planet. The actors chosen for each role were respectable, and Michael Fassbender in the role of David was a particularly good choice. The acting was incredible, and believable from all the actors, except for Guy Pearce who didn't manage to play his role as a power-obsessed, rich, businessman very well.

Although this movie is filled with random decisions made by the crew, and unanswered questions, I liked the movie very well, and found it very exciting from beginning to end. I would recommend watching this strongly, and would pass it on to a friend. A 8/10 from me.

  • 16 year old

The problem will always be that Ridley Scott was never going to be able to surpass Alien and as hard as the Prometheus bandwagon has tried to assure us it is not a prequel to Alien (which it is, lets be honest), that is ultimately what it is being viewed as and being held up to, therefore it was never going to live up to everyones expectations. Agreed it has no where near the suspense or original scares as Alien, but how could it and to be fair I don't think is what was being aimed for, I would recommend just going to see it with an open mind and just enjoy the ride, which compared to much of the tripe being churned out by Hollywood, is pretty darn good!

review:
Noomi Rapace has become an alien star becoming the role of the lone women of the story like that of Sigourney Weaver. Sweden's star really starting her big film star career playing 'Girl with a dragon Tattoo' films then working with Robert Downing and Jude Law starring in 'Sherlock Holmes: Game of Shadows'has shown the world stars can come from anywhere.

The film itself is a sci-fi film prequel to the classic Alien films which follows well with seen links to the previous Alien Films in it. Some of us would even call this a horror or thinking that it should be rated an 18 film, but the fact is that if they thought that this a scary film then they have definitely not seen the first Alien films where the story continues on from what happens in Prometheus. Can't wait for either Noomi Rapace and especially Ridley Scott's next film which I hope will be soon.

title: Prometheus review
review:
Hi everybody,

I went to see this movie with very high hopes, since i was very eager to see the prequel to my second favorite Sci-Fi franchise. My main hope was that this movie would re-ignite this awesome franchise which AVP (in my opinion) destroyed. Most things fulfilled my hopes, some minor ones did not... . The minor flaws iam talking about were mainly details that didn't made much sense, well... at least for people who've seen all the movies several times and know every detail there is to know about the Alien universe, otherwise these details would just pass the untrained eye without ever getting noticed.

Some of the major "+ points" for this movie were, e.g: - The acting that was very convincing at times and made it very easy for you to empathize with the characters. - The photography and cinematography were exactly what you would expect from a Ridley Scott movie, with very huge scenery, a set and costumes with very high detail and beautiful shots with great camera angles. - Good story build-up, by which i mean that you won't get dropped into the action immediately, but that time has been made to tell the story properly and build up the suspense towards the climax of the movie. - Very good special effects, some of the better work since Avatar, definitely worth seeing in 3D since it's filmed in 3D and not converted. - And lastly, a good "scaring" factor that keeps you hooked to your seat, although "horror" might not be the correct way to describe it.

Some of the flaws that i noticed in the details were mainly with the ship and its interior that you see in Alien (which ain't a spoiler, you can clearly see it in each trailer) and the life-cycle of the alien, because something about the cycle doesn't make sense to me, but you will notice it too when you go see the movie. Why does this bother me? because Ridley Scott made the first Alien movie himself, so i wonder why he overlooked those details.

Overall this movie did meet most of my expectations and iam sure that a sequel or even a trilogy might become the result of the open ending in this movie. However, i don't know what there is left to tell since the ending pretty much refers to the beginning of the first Alien movie.

title: A Sci-Fi Masterpiece and return to form for Ridley Scott
review:
Well, there are two or three clunky lines of dialog in the first half. Shame. That's about the only bad thing to be said about what is otherwise an immaculate science fiction film. From one of the most memorable opening sequences in recent memory to the cliffhanger at the end, Prometheus is a masterwork. After his disappointing revisionist take on Robin Hood, Ridley Scott is back in top form delivering his most beautiful film in years. Not since Christopher Nolan's Inception have audiences been treated to a science fiction this captivating and intelligent. I know it's become a cliché' to say this, but this really is a film where the special effects and CGI are built to compliment a story, characters, and theme. It's the same brand of visual storytelling found in Ridley Scott's best work.

I'll skip a synopsis as a courtesy to those attempting to go into this as fresh as possible, but know this: it's not the film some are expecting. This movie's goal isn't to fill in all the blanks in the Alien universe. It's a film about discussing ideas and raising questions, not all of which it chooses to answer. Yes, there's certainly room for a sequel if one is greenlit, but that's not the point. Prometheus explores a number of themes: the nature of discovery, the origin of life, the act of creation, the value of human existence, and the bleak universe in which we live. Of course some threads don't lead to anything conclusive. How can you expect one movie to provide solutions when the greatest minds in history have struggled with these very same notions?

I leave that for you to decide. Whatever you want to say about this movie, you can't deny the beauty and grandeur on display here. Ridley Scott and his artistic team paint a visual landscape on par with anything in Avatar. It may not be as lush and alive as the environments in Avatar, but the same level of attention and care went into the design and execution of Prometheus. One of thing that worried me prior to seeing this was the the possibility that the CGI creations would pale in comparison to the purely physical effects of Alien, but they take care to blend the two seamlessly. What shocked me the most was how immersive the 3D was. I'm usually quite sniffy about 3D, but the film makes such good use of it that part of me doesn't want to see it any other way. There is a scene about 30 minutes into the movie in which the research team first enters the cave containing the enormous head sculpture, the one we've all seen from the poster. There is a real sense of wonder and awe in scenes like this that completely floor me. I felt as if I was making profound discoveries right along side these giddy scientists. I was reminded of Werner Herzog's Cave of Forgotten Dreams, a fantastic documentary on cave paintings and dissecting the art and culture of our long-dead ancestors.

Plenty of people were greatly disappointed by this film, with accusations of bad scriptwriting, confusing narrative, poor character development, and unanswered questions. Question: are you insane? Have you been deprived of quality cinema for so long that you can't recognize it anymore? I genuinely can't understand the moaning and whinging that has been going on about this film, so I'm not going to address it further. For my money, Prometheus is the best movie 2012 has thus far given us. It's the quality of sci-fi that audiences want and deserve but rarely get anymore, with soul and pathos to support the eye-candy. And you know what? It was beaten at the weekend box office by Madagascar 3. Now I haven't seen Madagascar 3 – it could be wonderful – but unless it's an existential parable or a poetic dissection of the human spirit, I highly doubt it trumps Prometheus. If you haven't taken the time to watch this yet, do it. There is no reason for a widely released film of this caliber to go unseen. It is our obligation as cinema-goers to push this to its rightful place at the top of the box office charts. Think about it: how fantastic would it be to see a film this smart and artfully constructed at #1 next week? Even if you are one of the naysayers, admit it: you would rather see this at #1 than Rock of Ages, wouldn't you?

title: A different path in the Alien universe
review:
I was very lucky to see the film in the IMAX theater and like Scott's film Kingdom of Heaven, cinematography makes the film very beautiful.

The story looks into the origin of the human beings where the creation tries to find the creator. Many characters have personal agendas that range from noble to selfishness.

The actors played great and I love Guy's James Mason-like voice and how he could play an old frailed man. Mike as the android is just as creep like Ian's character from the original Aliens, and Miss Theron has that beautiful woman dark heart character.

In all, a great return to the Alien universe without the cheesy characters like in Aliens 3, 4, the versus Predator 1 and 2. Don't expect the movie to be gun shooting with bugs around, this is a film about searching for your long lost parents.

title: Linking "Prometheus" to "Alien"
review:
Warning: lots of spoilers and lots of speculation. By now I'm assuming you've read the summary so I'm not going to waste your time with another log-line. After racking my brain, here is my theory behind the science of "Prometheus" and exactly how this film is linked to the "Alien" universe. The film opens with a Mala'kak standing in front of a river, who we are told is an ancestor of humanoids, and some theorize, it committs ritual suicide by ingesting black liquid, which is actually the same liquid found in bomb like canisters manafacturered by the Mala'kak people. Once the Mala'kak drinks the liquid, this causes its body to disintegrate. Upon disintegration, its ashes fall into a riverbank and we witness its DNA deconstruct and give birth to a new strand of DNA.

My question is why if designed as a key ingredient to such a deadly weapon, would this be the same ingredient used to create human life? Now, we have to assume because a rescue beacon was present in the crashed Mala'kak ship found on LV-426 in "Alien", there is a rescue beacon present on the downed ship on LV-223. It's this distress signal from the downed Mala'kak ship on planet LV-223 (after Shaw and David launch), which eventually summons a Mala'kak rescue mission. Once touching ground on LV- 223, the rescue team encounters a hive of face-hugger's given birth to by the alien Xenomorph spawned from Shaw. The rescue team of Mala'kak make their escape, but not before the captain is attacked by a face-hugger and infected by the creature, eventually resulting in a "chest-bursting" episode. Unknowing the pilot is infected, they successfully take off from LV-223 (again, just my theory).

To further my theory, once the team of Mala'kak escapes from planet LV-223, the captain most likely begins to feel the monster from within and they are forced to crash-land on the closest planet: LV-426. This, resulting in the famous "space-jockey" chest-bursting image as seen in "Alien", further explaining the alien Xenomorph discovery on LV-426. Yes, Dallas believed the Mala'kak was fossilized, however, this is an impossible assessment due to the fact the Mala'kak on LV-426 was discovered in its space suit. This is just my theory anyway, but of course the sequel (if made) should have all of the answers, some possibly very different from the ones I arrived at.

title: People hate this just because its Alien connection and Mr. Scott
review:
Beside few missteps, like the old company boss and a bit confusing story, the movie is brilliant.

Beautiful to watch, interesting characters, great actors, never boring.

What can you expect more?

I got the impression that if this were an ordinary SiFi (without the Alien prequel and Ridley Scott fame), if this movie was from a newcomer director, everyone would clap their hands! :-)

If you watch the movie as a standalone story, not tied to Alien (Scott mentioned it is NOT a prequel, and I also share the opinion), you have 2 hours packed with fantastic action/adventure/horror.

Good thing the movie is 2 h long, not more. There is no time for boring dialog, long mission preparations etc. The movie movies quickly from one story point to another and leaves no room for boredom.

I watched the movie with friends and I agree at the end I was a bit confused and the whole engineer stuff, but those are minor drawbacks.

Folks, this is a story that stands on its own, forget Alien when you go watch the movie. Alien is in fact just Jaws in space and for me personally a bit boring and too dark.

Prometheus is way more fun to watch. You get: elements of adventure movies, where the crew explores the planet, elements of mystery, where they find the secret passages, you got humor (Alien series is way to serious folks!), great cast, fantastic action sequences, unique ideas, memorable scenes.

Go to the cinema without the "Scott made it, its an Alien prequel" thought and enjoy it, I did!

title: Prometheus is AWESOME!
review:
This is one of my favorite movies, and I really do not understand why people do not like it. I was born long after the Alien Anthology was released, so I do not share the same emotional connection that others do to the Alien movies, but I do enjoy the anthology and am just as big a fan as the next guy.

When I saw the preview for this movie, I was instantly intrigued. And I was not disappointed, in the movie itself or the connection to the Alien movies. Yes, the movie does have some parts that bug me (particularly where surgery is performed on Shaw to remove the impregnated alien).

Most of the characters are really great, except for a few of the geologists in the beginning who are thankfully killed off very early.

The movie is very suspenseful and action packed, and I was on the edge of my seat for every moment of it. Though it did not give me a better understanding of the Alien movies as I had hoped, it was a great movie nonetheless. I really look forward to the sequel to Prometheus!

title: Clever Scott
review:
Seeing this movie without doing the homework really does make it seem confusing and nonsensical at first. But Ridley Scott was truly seeking out the fans with this one, challenging the viewer to look deeper, and expand on what we thought we knew about the Alien universe and mythos. I remember seeing this film opening day and coming out of the cinema thinking "what". It just didn't click to me. I think the only satisfaction i got from the film was Elizabeth Shaw's transmission at the end. very reminiscent of lieutenant Elan Riply's at the end of the original Alien. But i was not fully compromised yet. I immediately started reading up on the film on forums and cinema cites. My curiosity could not take it anymore. I ended up seeing the movie two or three more times at the 3 dollar theater and it all started coming together. All of the clues became more blatant.

Like most movies these days, Prometheus has some minor flaws that fans and critics love to point out and pick at. But personally it doesn't add up. don't let these clichés mislead you. this movie is smart and fun, if you have someone to guide you thorough the esoteric and cryptic clues. Prometheus is film with truly more to it than some might think. this Film is about two scientists who believe they have stumbled across the very clue that will reveal the mysteries of mans origin and touches upon themes such as creation, insignificance,science and even religion. However one flaw that i simply couldn't let fly was the lack of connection between the crew members. their always seemed to be forced hostility and disrespect. At one point i was actually hoping for some of these characters demise. you simply don't care for most of them. The dialogue is pretty lifeless sometimes, even when something very important and interesting is being said. However there are some performances that are actually key to the film, more notably the character David, an android crew member played by Michael Fassbender. He is mono toned in everything he says, but when he talks, believe me you listen.

liking Noomi Rapace as Elizabeth Shaw was actually a build-up process. but once the stakes were high and the suspense built up, i was saying "GO SHAW". She has a great scene that surely lives up the notoriety of the chest burster scene in the Original Alien and will be remembered if anything. Her dialogue is delivered well and energetically, and she really does creates a believable curious scientist on the verge of discovering the origins of mankind.

So don't be put off by the fan-boys still comparing it to the original. It proudly stands alone and is actually a very smart and creative film. but if you love understanding movies and don't mind doing a little reading, i truly recommend checking out "Chariots of the Gods" by Erich von Däniken.

title: Really, really, really stupid
review: Is this considered a spoiler? Do not pay to see this film. This movie is a huge piece of crap. How could a movie with this many big name actors, a huge budget, and Ridley Scott add up to a mostly unwatchable sci-fi absurdity? After watching it I couldn't even tell you what it was about. None of the characters were worth investing even the remotest bit of interest. It was like Scott was trying to make a blend of Aliens and Avatar and even if he did who the hell would want to see that movie considering that Avatar was a blend of Lord of the Rings and Dances with Wolves? I can only hope that this thing is/will be a huge flop at the box office. And IMDF doesn't allow profanity? Is it a movie review site or a religious organization? How could anyone old enough to read be offended by a word?

title: Ridley Scott's visual/sci-fi/horror masterpiece
review: First let me start off by saying i don't understand the anonymous hate given to this movie it was truly epic on every single aspect. From the opening scene to the scene where the space jockey flipped out this groundbreaking sci-fi epic distributed state of the art visual effects, Oscar worthy performances, grisly images, truly mesmerizing IMAX 3D that left me breathless. To me this movie succeeded on every level and could have even been perfection but it had its flaws (every movie has flaws except for the dark knight, district 9, AVATAR, and black swan). Michael Fassbender, Charlize Theron, and Noomi Rapace give breathtaking performances. Any fans of a truly amazing movie that requires thinking and mind blowing visuals watch P R O M E T H E U S. Its a must see i will be getting on Blu ray and thats my short review (saw it on opening day in IMAX 3D twice).

title: Beautifully photographed nonsense
review: Having all the Alien films "burdening" my back (and I still think only the first - which should also be the last as a true masterpiece and a SF par excellence - and partly Mr. Fincher's third were good, involving Dan O'Bannon as a scriptwriter in both cases), I've entered this film expecting Mr. Scott's expertise on the matter, his unique aesthetic approach and a good psychological study of humans in unusual helpless circumstances. Instead of that here we have a mess. No science whatsoever (starship rumbling in open space, hyper-advanced robot, yet C4 method of determining age and so on), no character in characters, parts almost randomly put together creating an illusion of continuity etc. It does not seem like Mr. Scott at all. More like some infantile producers with lots of money and lack of brain. And the story has such a potential. Cast is also excellent but wasted for nothing. We could get so many answers from this movie but instead we got a question - why? Five stars for camera work/photography, Mr. Scott's struggle to get something that makes sense out of this and the cast. Everything else, less than -273 degrees Celsius.

title: Disappointed
review:
The best of this movie is actually, that I started to read the negative reviews here: and a lot of them made me just laugh, because of so many true remarks about this movie. Really, Mr. Scott, I am a big fan of your films. But this one... I don't get it, why the IMDb-rating in total is now at 7,5...

I mean: Its okay to go for the big adventure, and graphics are adequate, but why is this story so flat?, the characters so underdeveloped?, the references to Alien (and alike) so cheap?, the acting mostly so horribly uninspired?, or pretentiously overinspired...

And there sooo many details just no right: F.i., the old guy with so much money and even more hope (way too much make up btw), he just crawls over there to get a bump from the "Founder" and that's it? That would be fine in a comedy, but here? Or the landing on the distant planet: found the place to be right away, after such a journey. Would it not have been much nicer, to create some tension for the viewer by making it a bit more difficult to find this place? Or the pregnant girl: just gets this rough surgery, then staples, to walk/work on? And the whole crew: big mission and then such a bunch of weirdos? Enough, I jump to the end of the movie: seems pretty much like we have to fear part 2. I just hope for the better... maybe we get some answers, if the Founder in the opening scene was a Prometheus, and if forced or however... but please: Mr. Scott, get at least a better script-writer!

title: Completed nonsense - a major disappointment
review:
I was quite looking forward to seeing this movie. I am a huge fan of science fiction and have been for almost 30-years. The previews really had me sold. Wow - can I just say that I must myself have been in another dimension in thinking this would be good. There were moments that I thought I had just about had enough nonsense and was ready to walk away. But, for some reason, I thought there might be a major turn of events that I didn't want to miss. That never happened.

The story line created no suspense, thrill, or intrigue. Knowing later that is is based off of the "Aliens" movies, I can say that it really didn't fit.

The only thing I liked was the design and tech of the ship (Prometheus). the cinematography was also quite engaging. However, I wasn't watching this movie just to see all the cool designs and effects. I hoped to discover a point to this movie, and perhaps find myself hoping to continue the journey, with a part 2, but the journey ended for me as soon as the credits rolled. Oh well... Live and learn.

title: Follows the structure of Alien and the philosophy of Blade Runner
review:
It Looks like Ridley Scott successfully copied the theme and the form of his two beloved classics: Alien and Blade Runner into a new movie called Prometheus.

The movie has a familiar story of Alien: a team is sent to look for Extraterrestrial life in another planet. Of course things go wrong and (...)

We have some philosophical descent from Blade Runner with questions like who are we? why are we here? where are we going?. The scientist try to answer these questions with this big mission.

The movie has the great suspense like Alien has, we have here a new "Ripley" called Elizabeth Shaw (Noomi Rapace) and in the end we truly can make Prometheus relative to Alien.

In the end it came out a great Science Fiction and Ridley Scott's earlier movies now can live on the present.

title: It could be better, it could be more believable...
review:
Pros : Great landscapes, natural look, not CG, great design of alien interiors.

Cons : too much, too unbelievable scenes :

SPOILER :

1) they care about atmosphere chemical composition, but they ignore potential biohazard and take their helmets off.

2) Alien growth is unbelievably fast. Noomi Rapace learns that she is pregnant with alien, so she undergo an abortion on automated surgery device - when she strips off, her belly is flat, when machine takes out the alien fetus it looks like weighting 10 kg or more... The fetus remains in operating chamber and after one day it is big as elephant - what have it eaten there to grow so fast ? Bandages ? Iodine ? This is just STUPID! Noomi Rapace after abortion (removing of 10kg alien) has a 20 cm cut in her belly but she is fit enough to go to aliens ship in after 2 hours, and to run and jump like wind after few more hours. Buhaha !

3) Huge Alien ship is rammed by Prometheus ship, collision looks like taking place at 50km/h. Alien ship drops from altitude of more than 1km, but when it hurts the ground it is pretty much intact. Even the android head inside the alien ship remains unhurt in the same place... Total nonsense. If Alien ship would be so fragile (no force field) to be destroyed by the collision with Prometheus, it would transform to dust when hitting the ground.

4) Android Dave is learning hindu, and after those lessons he is able to read alien texts, to unlock alien secret codes and communicate with aliens... And to operate their ship. LOL !

5) They land on a random spot on alien planet (they didn't knew where to look for aliens)and they land exactly where aliens base was...

6) Trip from earth took 2.5 year, when the closest star system is 4 light years from earth.

7) Aliens were engineering quite bizarre weapons on the planet (monsters) instead of making just some simple viruses or just nukes (cheaper, easier, more efficient)

8) Prometheus aerodynamic shape would make it burn when entering atmosphere (it even haven't decelerated from lightspeed)

9) IQ and mentality of most of team members is closer to one you could expect from a plumber or gangster than a member of space mission to another planet costing billions $.

10) Having a light inside helmet looks cool, but it would prevent the guy inside to see what is around (due to light reflexes on glass - if you don't believe, try to drive your care with interior light during the night)

11) DNA of Alien Engineers is identical to contemporary humans - so why chimpanzees DNA is 98% similar to human? Were chimpanzees, Neanderthals, gibbons and Australopithecus also engineered by aliens - and what about mice and cats ? We share a LOT of DNA with all lifeforms on earth. The whole idea that humans were engineered by aliens to be exactly like aliens is a pure nonsense. ------------

But it could be worse - the plus is that they don't speak English with aliens (as it would be the case in Star Trek ;-) ) They use their pressure suits and helmets sometime (as it wouldn't be the case in Star Wars) And there are no laser guns shots.

In all it is the best, the most spectacular move from Alien series, better than Star Wars, better than Avatar, but it is not near close to Kubrick Space Odyssey 2001. Sadly too dumb. Too much bang, not enough thought and spirit.

title: Great Sci-fi and set-up for a sequel
review:
I thoroughly enjoyed this film and everyone is entitled to their opinion, but there are some very harsh reviews on here nit picking with every little detail.

The scale of the film is impressive with some of the scenes being breath taking.

The aspects of the film that I loved most is the fact that it doesn't answer very many question, leaves a lot more questions to be answered and more importantly requires the audience to figure out certain sequence of events that occur well before Prometheus has landed on LV-223.

I hate been force fed plots etc so this film ticked all the boxes for me.

Oh and just a note: see the film twice as you will see much more the second time round

title: Underrated Excellence
review:
As aforementioned, this film is underrated excellence. Sir Ridley Scott intended to create a masterpiece and he has done nothing short of it. Sure Prometheus may not be as good as the first Alien, but it is definitely a masterpiece in its own right when compared to other lesser sci-fi movies of today. The first thing in the move you will notice are the spectacular visuals and these visuals have to go down as some of the best alongside those in Blade Runner, another Ridley sci-fi classic. It's worth watching in 2-D as the 3-D doesn't add much to it, but it only adds towards straining your eyes. There may be some instances where you think that the script has been 'speechified', as in the script is unnatural however, most of this is done by the Android, David, so you would expect a robot to be slightly better and more literate than a normal human being. The acting in the movie is phenomenal, with the Noomi Rapace and Michael Fassbender stealing the show with breathtaking brilliance but the side characters, over a dozen of them don't add much to the plot or the movie, nor do they get enough face time like we'd seen in the previous alien films. The music in the film is also another excellent piece that adds to the feeling of suspense and thrill and Ridley Scott has really used the music to make the movie a masterpiece.

Sure it isn't Alien, but Prometheus is a lot different to it as well and is definitely worth a watch, you're money is worth it...well, only in 2D.

title: The brief science fiction resurrection
review:
Ridley Scott cut the anticipation on June 1st releasing the eagerly awaited Prometheus to cinematic screens everywhere.

Noomi Rapace, Michael Fassbender and Charlize Theron lead a promising cast in this Sci-fi whirl-wind exploring once again, the genre that brought Ridley Scott's ego to light.

Elizabeth Shaw (Rapace) and Charlie Holloway (Logan Green) spend their days exploring caves and landscapes seeking clues, leading to conspiracies, leading to self-belief of the numerous possibilities and unanswered questions behind mankind's creation. Their obsessive will for exploration pays off when they discover what they believe is the key direction to the life-form that walked before us. The loved up pair can't help but accept a thousand year old carving to be an open invitation to join whatever it may be they seek.

Prometheus is the holding vessel carrying a crew of numerous qualifications. The Journey through space is constructed by Shaw and Holloway, with both of them being the navigational system to the universe they are destined to arrive in. Idris Elba plays Janek, the captain of Prometheus. A strong character, ever so careful as to why he, as well as others should risk their life believing in Shaw's ambitions.

Meredith (Theron) is on board for one reason only, to see the journey out safe while so obviously wanting nothing to do with the desires of both Holloway and Shaw. From what Meredith can see, this is a far-fetched idea and a pointless journey...how wrong she was about to be. Theron is once again the bitch in the movie. Sure why not? she plays it ever so sexy!.

The journey through one universe to the other leads Prometheus into a battle that could change history. Upon an amazing discovery through the ambitious Shaw and Holloway, their mysterious yet expected find leads the ship and crew into a fight not only for their own lives, but the lives of others.

Prometheus is a brilliant sci-fi movie as Michael Fassbender helps by leading the movie to the enjoyment it Deserves. Introducing his robotic character, David. He is constructed by Peter Weyland to have as much interaction and affiliation with a human, as one human would be to another. His hilarious, soulless body is well created to the point where the viewer believes in Fassbenders' desire to act. David is the back-Bone to the ship, as the crew appear unfastened to rest their lives in his hands. A darker side to Fassbenders' character is surprisingly exciting, giving Prometheus tense interactions both on and off the vessel.

Prometheus is as mysterious as the trailer makes it out to be. Ridley Scott does fantastic in returning to the concept of Aliens, but not "Alien". Just like his previous movies, without naming the obvious, Ridleys' way of creating likable characters is still smartly written with his latest work appearing highly nostalgic. The audience will realize the ship descending into the unknown and where you will once again find yourself rooting for certain characters to make it home. There are always individuals on board who you know are either too arrogant or unqualified to be on such a mission. Prometheus does well in offering the audience a general mix of personalities.

However, it does, like most movies with a great introduction reveals some loose ends with an explanation much needed if Ridley Scott was to return for a Prometheus sequel. The first 100 minutes or so are quite tense and does well in keeping the audience attention and anticipating a possible unforgettable climax. Prometheus will disappoint some fans on the basis of what I and most would believe to be a highly rushed ending to the movie. The production just seemed to run out of ideas in the last 20 minutes or so. Maybe that is the appropriate result and much deserved outcome for a film that got the wrong attention and anticipation and seemed to have manipulated fans awaiting its release ever since its first statement which claimed Prometheus to be a prequel to alien...

There is so much to be said about Ridleys' return, but so much the audience must answer for themselves. Prometheus is an all-round bloody good sci-fi movie. A concept not too original but fans of the Alien saga will enjoy without having to connect any apparent dots.

A prequel originally, but I believe Ridley Scott himself fails to agree. Prometheus is its own concept, with some convenient characters. A must see for all Sci-fi fans. A return to chilling torture in outer space that no other director would dare to challenge. Oh except for James Cameron. :)

Did you enjoy my review? check out my previous and up to date reviews at my blog - http://gerrysreviewsforthosecurious.blogspot.com

title: Interesting...
review:
First off, the film looks stunning, Ridley Scott has a great eye and all of his films look fantastic. I saw the film in 2D and I still thought it looked great (I won't join in the 3D debate here).

There has been a lot of debate about whether this is a prequel to Ridley Scott's film 'Alien' (1979). Well, I have it on good authority that it pre-dates that film and the planet they land on is not the one depicted in that film. In fact, I've heard Scott say in interview that there's enough material for two more films to bring us up to the point where 'Alien' starts. But I digress, personally, I found the film quite engrossing and some of the ideas about the origins of life on Earth very interesting. Yes, there are parallels to be drawn between this as 'Alien', but even so, I found the faster pace and the visuals did just enough to make up for any weaknesses in the plot. You have to remember that its fantasy and its entertainment, as soon as you start to take it too seriously you're probably going to be disappointed. I was prepared to go with it and consequently very much enjoyed the experience. Would I watch it again, hell yes!... RECOMMENDED.
