title: A sort-of-but-not-really prequel to Alien.
review:
Mix a fairly straightforward story of murderous aliens with deep, metaphorical themes about the creation of the human race, and what do you get? Apparently, you get a confusing mess. Prometheus, the so-called prequel to Alien, is a tad too ambitious for its own good, bringing up far too many questions and ideas that it neither answers nor follows up on. The film's cast is a group of largely unlikeable characters, with the exception of a brilliantly-acted android. The movie was directed by the accomplished Ridley Scott, so of course the movie looks gorgeous, but that's one of the only things it's got going for it. If you're anticipating a welcome return to the Alien franchise, then you've still got some waiting to do.

From the opening scene of the film, it's clear that Prometheus is a bit of a mixed bag. It becomes very obvious that the story is going to revolve primarily around an original science fiction idea, with no more than a few nods to the Alien mythology. The title of the movie is revealed segment by segment, like the first Alien, but that's just about as much similarity as the two films share. If you're paying good attention and you know your stuff, you may find some Alien Easter eggs to appease you, but they are few and far between until the climax of the film.

This leaves the rest of the two-and-a-half hour running time to explain no less than the origins of humanity. Naturally this leads to many profound and thought-provoking questions; but the kicker is that the movie never answers them. This is what's so disappointing, infuriating, and ultimately underwhelming about it. So many questions, big or small, are left unexplained, rendering the entire movie, in many ways, pointless. I hear that the prequel sequel to the prequel (?) will act as a second act to this film and answer these questions for us, which I would absolutely love. But as a standalone film, Prometheus really falls short in the storytelling department. It aches for resolution.

There are also a few problems with the cast in this movie: either they're unlikeable, or their characters are just plain dumb-asses. The main character Elizabeth Shaw, portrayed by Noomi Rapace, is annoying. There's no other way to describe her. This is my own personal opinion here, and everyone else may feel differently, but her naivety, stupidity, and lack of a character arc made her a pretty obnoxious character. Her boyfriend was also stupid and annoying, and wasn't acted very well. I also found myself eagerly anticipating the deaths of the equally obnoxious supporting cast. Idris Elba, Guy Pierce, and Charlize Theron gave serviceable performances in their respective roles. Michael Fassbender as the android David 8 was by far the best part of the film, and he completely stole the show.

Moreover, the movie looked amazing. The special effects were top-notch, the cinematography was inspired and beautiful, and the movie had some haunting and memorable imagery. This is a Ridley Scott film after all; he's pretty damn good at this. The creature design was fantastic, the humanoid aliens looked cool, and the futuristic technology was awesome. The aforementioned opening scene, though lacking explanation, was breathtaking to look at. The 3D added some depth, but is definitely not necessary.

Once this film receives a sequel, I have a feeling we'll all like Prometheus a lot more. In fact, it may go on to become a science fiction classic. But right now, this movie doesn't stand well on its own two feet. I give it an optimistic 6 out of 10 stars.

title: Explaining Prometheus, my take
review:
I say Ridley Scott is an avant-garde in the context of a continuum of modern sci-fi film-making. It begins with Kubrick's 2001: A Space Odyssey (1968) and then, only after nearly a decade of Planet of the Apes (1968) sequels, moves on to Lucas' Star Wars and Spielberg's Close Encounters of the Third Kind (1977), before Alien (1979) and The Empire Strikes Back (1980) and finally Bladerunner, The Thing and E.T.: the Extra-Terrestrial (1982), which make the genre more popular until Cameron's The Terminator (1984) and Aliens (1986) come along and blow it up.

Ridley Scott was avant-garde during the first two decades of multi-episode, scalar, sci-fi sagas. He is a visionary filmmaker with a unique and very specific blueprint: a slow build with the first half of a film to establish grand settings and an ensemble of characters within an immense context and then a hell ride for the second half of the film to its fantastic, terrorizing conclusion.

The Grand Plot Begins on Earth Before the Dawn of Man Human life on Earth began millennia ago because a being - perhaps twice human-size, capable of interstellar travel and to whom we refer hereafter as an Engineer - drank something toxic and died while visiting Earth, collapsing into a waterfall.

It is made clear in the title sequence, this Engineer's DNA co-mingled with the primordial soup to jump start evolution and ultimately to create us: smaller, weaker, less advanced versions of the Engineers. It is unclear whether this is a purposeful act, but the pain the Engineer endures in disintegrating implies not.

2089 A.D., Humans Discover the Engineers A series of ancient cave paintings are found all over Earth, each depicting one of these over-sized human figures (the Engineers) pointing upward to a constellation pattern. In the year 2089, archaeologist couple Elizabeth Shaw and her boyfriend Charlie Holloway discover this star map among the remnants of several otherwise unconnected ancient cultures. The two interpret this as an invitation from humanity's forerunners - an interpretation which may or may not be one of many misreadings in the grand narrative.

Ridley Scott has succeeded in imbuing contemporary human hubris onto our future behavior, making viewers unsure whether the actions and opinions of any of his characters, except Ripley, are sound.

The events of the film Prometheus take place between 2089 and 2094. Shaw and Holloway are hired to lead an expedition to the theorized location depicted in the cave drawings,a moon that orbits the immense ringed-planet LV-223. They travel via cryogenic suspension and interstellar travel with the crew of the ship USS Prometheus.

2093, the Prometheus plot Peter Weyland, the elderly founder and CEO of the Weyland Corporation, funds the creation of the scientific deep space research vessel USS Prometheus to follow the cave painting maps to a distant moon orbiting the planet LV-223, many light years from Earth.

The ship's crew travels in stasis at light speed while the android David stays awake, pilots the craft, studies ancient languages to translate for possible interactions with humanity's makers, and monitors the passengers in cryo-sleep on their voyage, going so far as to read their dreams.

Note: One flaw noted is that if LV-223 is, as stated, many light years away and the Prometheus arrives in just over two years, the craft must have traveled faster than the speed of light to cross the distance in space between Earth and LV-223. This remains unexplained and mere cryo-stasis is not sufficient to explain it. It can only be a maximum of two light years away.

The android David, the scientist Shaw and the CEO Weyland are direct parallels as characters to the androids Ash and Bishop; to Ripley; and to the Company in the Alien films. These tropes are significant on multiple levels because Scott makes use of the image we have of these characters - he constructs them to be knocked about so we can see a range of human experience - and in so doing, he acknowledges, subtly, sci-fi of the past.

In David, one senses not only Ash and Bishop, but also the cold, insouciant, horrifying spirit of HAL from Kubrick's 2001: A Space Odyssey; in Shaw, the naive wonderment of Jodie Foster's Ellie Arroway in Contact meets Ripleys stubborn righteousness; and in Weyland, we've the aging hubris of Jurassic Park's Jon Hammond, played so deliciously by Richard Attenborough, coupled with the billionaire boys' club attitude and ever-forward pushing of Contact's S.R. Hadden, as played by Jon Hurt Here, Weyland is portrayed by Guy Pierce as a cold, calculating and demanding CEO, inventor (of David) and an aging corporate raider obsessed with extending his own life above all other concerns.

In Prometheus, there's continuity of feeling with Alien and Aliens, and nuanced shades of many science fiction films and characters of the recent past, but there remains a doomed feeling throughout that much of our human spirit is weak and flawed. Maybe that's why people don't like it.

The principle criticism I hear from fans so far, who like the work in general, is that the characters are not developed. Very few of the characters are given depth, and it's painfully obvious that the "Hollywood Summer Blockbuster" cut is brutal. One has to imagine a lot, and much if it isn't good. That's not easy and folks don't like doing it. Ridley, the avant garde, expects a little more than most.

That said, the relationship between Shaw and Holloway is the most explored. It's revealed that she has faith in Christ and that he is an atheist. More, that in making their discovery Holloway chides Shaw about her faith. She claims to be unfazed, a believer. This, is what Weyland saw in her ...

title: In the IMDb Prometheus page no one can read your review!
review:
Next up in the highly anticipated summer blockbuster film line up is Ridley Scott's semi prequel to 1979's Alien, Prometheus an ambitious sci-fi adventure seeking some of mankind's burning questions. Unlike the previous Alien films this raises a bigger sense of discovery then an all out gore –fest instead focusing on this all important expedition for mankind's maker and is all the more complex as a result. This is a hard film to wrap my brain around mostly because of the mix of a complex premise of finding our maker with a sci-fi horror movie.

Prometheus is an intriguing film with Scott creating this ambiguous mythology that really heightens the sense of mystery and awe. This is defiantly the films highlight with the film going at a slow pace to build up in this extraordinary adventure. Information is slowly dispersed to us from the ancient markings that our female protagonist Elizabeth Shaw (played by Noomi Rapace what a name) finds in a cave to the exploration of the planet, to the realisation of what they have really discovered. Once Shaw and her crew land on the planet the sense of unknown is really heightened by parking the ship next to the alien ship and constantly returning to and from the ship, Prometheus and the alien spaceship does show the inquisitive and slightly apprehensiveness of the crew on-board the Prometheus.

Another great aspect of the movie is the overall look of the movie. Scott is usually great at making grand worlds for his characters to inhabit such as Blade Runner and Gladiator. What is really a breath of fresh air is the sparing use of CGI to create a naturalistic world. The visuals from this are all very traditional sci-fi accept with a super budget to make it all possible. The soundtrack also captures the sense of wonderment and has a very Jurassic Park feel to it.

What I found to be the major problem with this film was the lacklustre screenplay by Damon Lindelof in which I could predict what the characters would say before they said it. Side Characters also don't leave there designated stereotypes and have little interaction and development. It is like Lindelof can't be bothered to develop these characters because we know they will be alien chow but the point is to make these characters interesting so we become attached to them so we don't want them to become alien chow. At other times some characters lack passion for the expedition there on which makes no sense why would you fly halfway across the galaxy for something they have no enthusiasm for did they lose a bet or something? It is slightly embarrassing that the film with spandex wearing heroes has more of an engaging script. However the main characters are engaging enough especially David the android (played by Michael Fassbender) despite his confusing motivation he was an interesting character providing an enigmatic view on his agenda who I feel deserves more screen time but he quit while he was ahead :P.

A further gripe is the disappointing resolution where the film just ends abruptly with the hope that the remaining questions will be explained in further sequels.

In conclusion Prometheus is hit and miss fans of the alien films will most likely be disappointed but if you're not a fan or just a fan of Ridley Scott's auteur then it is worth checking out. Overall Prometheus is a solid film with its unique atmosphere and striving story but the side characters don't merge with the fantastical world they are on and the film is just building up to more build up. 7/10

title: Disappointing
review:
A truly promising beginning to the film with some excellent questions being asked about religion and some intriguing ideas about us being "engineered" by an alien race very similar to ourselves (see Space Jockey in Alien). The story continued quite well with good suspense, excellent acting and superb visuals. Some of the best visuals I've seen to be honest, first film I've seen since 2009 that I though had better visuals than Abram's Star Trek. Unfortunately it seems as though the writers of Prometheus decided that this superb introduction to the story didn't deserve a real ending, and copped out of addressing any of the questions raised earlier, while Scott resorts to some visually disturbing horror to keep us interested. I wouldn't criticize this element if it wasn't so very similar to the horror of Alien. This coupled with the (unfortunately) expected ending of Rapace's character being the sole survivor (unless you count androids of course) is also annoyingly similar to Alien. The difference of course being that while Ripley in Alien is a truly sympathetic and lovable character, Rapace's character isn't likable enough for me to even remember her name.

The annoying cop out ending, coupled with some references to Alien without serving as a good prequel (see screenrant's article on how the filmmakers could have made it one, you'll see it had potential as a cheap, moneymaking prequel, which unfortunately would be better than the real life result), and very little in the area of character development leads this work to be less of a pseudo Alien prequel that stands on its own and more of a bad reboot which tries and fails to copy the elements of the groundbreaking Alien series. This coupled with the disappointing Robin Hood and the surprising decision for a Blade Runner sequel, shows us that Scott is just not the man he used to be.

Prometheus receives six stars only for its stunning visuals, excellent exposition and good acting (as good as it could be with such flat characters)

title: Unsatisfying and unanswered questions only saved by settings and directions.
review:
When I go to the cinema I sometimes find it really hard to switch off and just enjoy a film. I'm finding more and more that when I go to watch something, I put my critical head on and think about finding negatives and positives. Alas I did the same with this film. For those of you not in the know, Prometheus is set in the same world as the "Alien" films, a semi-prequel. A couple of explorers found clues to the origins of mankind and embark on a quest to find "answers" as to who and why we were created. The company funding the trip is Weyland (the same company who feature in the Alien universe) and a select group of scientists and company employees go in search and find the meaning of life.

Much is expected from this film and I for one, am one of those who could not wait to see it. As a big fan of the Alien films, I had high expectations, but when it came out and there were whispers of it not being anything more than a big sci fi film which happens to co exists in the same world as the great films that preceded it, I was apprehensive. It wasn't an alien film....but in it's defence, Ridley Scott has always claimed that this is a standalone film which echoes from the Alien universe.

The main problem I had with it is the fact I feel the film uses it's links to the classic films to garner audiences to go and see it. I don't think the film would have had a big budget or the director if it was just another science fiction film. Is the film any good though? Well, it's not bad but it's not great. It is lacking in thrills and suspense but has some interesting ideas. I enjoyed it but I had many reservations with character's and some few plot points/holes.

The film's characters are sketchily drawn, only a few are given more depth and personality while others just stand and look on in awe. With Noomi Rapace's character (Elisabeth Shaw) she is feisty and a survivor and the main protagonist so comparison will undoubtedly be made to Ripley. The only other character to have any depth would be the android David played with cool calmness by Michael Fassbender. Unfortunately the others are all forgettable and lack any real emotional connection.

A personal frustration I encountered with this film is that throughout numerous questions are raised but most are left unanswered. There is little or no clear resolution. The ambiguity throughout allows for viewers to interpreter their own answers and reasons to why things happen, which some may like but does little for me. It clearly has the stamp of 'Lost' (writer and co-creator Damon Lindelof is on script duties) all over the narrative. The motives of the engineers (the space jockey from Alien) are never clear, and neither is David. It leads to an unsatisfying feeling.

On the positive note, the location and cinematography is superb (but I never expected it not to be). The attention to detail on the ship is magnificent and the mood and lighting effects are in keeping with the Alien universe. There is clearly a deliberate attempt at making the film echo it's predecessors in tone as well as in it's dialogue, and that gives the film a sense of the familiar and allows the audience to feel comfortable in it's setting.

One feels that this film would not of had the excitement or expectations if the film was not set in the same universe, but then it's kind of hard to see this working without it. Many of you would no doubt do the same and make comparison to the other films, but it's unfair to do so and to watch it without thinking of the other films is really hard. In fact all this films does is make me want to watch Alien again.

title: OK - not bad - not great
review: I was, like many of you, looking forward to this movie. I'm a sci-fi movie fan, the bottom line of which means I've sat through a lot of dross over the years hoping against hope that THIS movie will match up (or at least come close) to the 'classics' like Bladerunner, Alien or one of the better Trek movies (see my standards aren't sky high). I didn't HATE this movie (the opening scene was wonderfully 'mystical') and the way the whole movie shot is also stunning. The plot though -hmmm. It *is* a prequel - I got that much by myself, and it *does* give us a little insight into the 'space jockeys' (I didn't feel it did them a horrid disservice) and the creatures they had decided to replace uswith. My issues came with the silly things (the ending), and the 2 dimensional characters about whom we are supposed to care. I cared very much about Ellen Ripley (even in the dire Alien 4), but not so much about Dr Shaw. The Android David was the only person I came close to wondering about (and why didn't they make a bigger deal about the sibling rivalry between him and Theron's character?). Guy Pearce was wasted as the overly made up old geezer. Some reviewers have said for them this movie was themed around 'sacrifice' - however for me I got 'bad ideas'. It was a bad idea for the Space Jockeys too replace us with a life-form that turned on them. They were smart enough to create mini-space jockeys (us) but not smart enough to test out the proto-aliens (they made thousands of DNA-modules containing their essence) before they realised their creations were rapacious killers only intent on reproducing. It was a bad idea for the scientists to NOT wonder why the ship they got was full of mostly NON science types. I twas a bad idea for the old guy to 'allow' his daughter to go on the trip - and put her in charge. He says during the movie that 'she came anyway' but he's the BOSS of a HUGE corporation - he could've prevented it (even though she thought he was dead) It was a bad idea to not learn more about the moon before landing on it. It was a bad idea to let people get on the ship before seeing if they were infected (if your crew mate is folded into an origami frog, its a bad idea OK?) Having said all that - I totally understood why Shaw wanted to talk to the SJs - even if just to say 'wtf guys? you seriously thought those creatures were BETTER than us?' I understood why David allowed the pregnancy - he was under orders from old-made-up guy to find the secret of eternal life and this seemed like a good opportunity. I didn't understand why he didn't mention her obvious removal of the alien life-form though. He just looks slightly annoyed about it. As for squid baby growing on no food - I thought that was obvious too - it grew to a 3 month size in 10 hours, it was designed to just GROW until it found a host. Overall the film asked more questions than it answered - that's OK I'm used to that but still, it was a bit of a let down. The script guys need a caning though - the dialogue was pretty dire at times. I have to say I was disappointed overall - but its not a horrible movie - its just not as great as it COULD have been. Even if you go into this with no expectations (and that's hard considering the trailers being everywhere, whetting our appetites) its still a bit of a let down (and this is from someone who really liked Starship troopers).

title: Prometheus: A Movie that should not have been a Prequel
review:
Set in the 2090's in Earth years, "Prometheus" set out to try and recreate the style of horror from Ridley Scott's "Alien" and attempt to reveal more lore in the Alien saga. Visually, the movie is quite stunning to watch with many gorgeous and gory scenes which are well, and in some cases too well, detailed. I am happy to say that computer generated scenes are restricted to a small portion of the movie and that most of the sets are fully fleshed out and made from scratch, including many of the interiors, which I must give the carpenters credit for. This does not cover the fact that the story itself has several major and minor plot-holes.

The major plot hole I am disappointed with lies in a convoluted B-Story. This story involves David the Android, Dr. Shaw, Dr. Shaw's boy friend, and the last remaining Humanoid Alien (which apparently created all life on Earth). David becomes disappointed and presumably homicidal when he hears his creator, Dr. Weyland, say that he has no soul and is not truly his son. This in concert with other humans putting him down leads him to want to take revenge on the humans. He does this by taking a sample of black goo found in one of the many vases found inside the alien compound and uses it to secretly poison Dr. Shaw's boyfriend just before they "do the nasty." This black goo kills Dr. Shaw's boyfriend by disintegrating his body. Apparently, it had already affected his sperm and there is now a squid growing inside Dr. Shaw. She get's an emergency C-Section which tosses out the baby squid and she then leads to attempt to disinfect/kill it by leaving the room and pressing a button to clear out the room. She thinks its dead, but after most of the events, she returns to this last remaining part of the ship to try and last out until help picks her up, finding something still in that chamber, but locked safely away. Unfortunately, the last humanoid Alien attempts to kill her in revenge for thwarting his plans. This leads to her opening the chamber with said squidly to reveal the little squidly turned into BIG GIANT SQUIDLY which proceeds to attack the humanoid, giving Shaw time to run for it. The squid then shoves an appendage into the humanoids mouth and kills it. We can assume this is the first face huger, which is apparently a bastardized child. Just before the credits, we see the body of the humanoid which is pulsating and then ejects a small creature which turns out to be the Alien we all know and love... So facehugers were made from a diseased human and a normal human, and the Alien was made from a face huger and a face raped humanoid?

That's almost as bad as George Lucas's excuse for how Darth Vader came to be.

Overall, "Prometheus" is enjoyable, but Ridley Scott did a horrible job of incorporating Alien into it. It should not have been established as a prequel to the original and should have been a stand alone movie.

title: Objectified Review
review:
Being a hardcore Alien fan, I felt the urge to write a review first time in my life after seeing the film last night. Maybe my biggest disappointment was caused by my high expectations, since I need to be honest, it has been a long time since we last seen a good sci-fiction movie. So, with all the premises that the film brought, Ridley Scott as being the director, good cast, amazing trailers and propaganda online, and decent budget, I thought this film might answer some of my questions (not on life!) so I gave it a shot. To be frank, it's a decent film and it's worth seeing in the theater and it's definitely not below 7/10! The film deserves a decent rating, but it should be also criticized so that promising writers like Damon Lindelof and Jon Spaihts would do a better job next time, if they will still be involved. I have seen other movies and works of Lindelof before like Lost, Star Trek and Cowboy's and Aliens. And I have a feeling that he knows how a plot works for a film with commercial goals. That's the main problem with Prometheus as everyone expected it to be a 'masterpiece' but surely it isn't and it won't be after the sequels to come with the destruction of such phenomenal concepts.

From the beginning of the film I was really into it, with the images that were being shown (especially the volcanic rock formations which is also grounded in philosophy since earth spits lava to create life) were highly moving. Although the search is on 'origins of life', the colors are set to dark tones to create an overall horrific atmosphere. If you know Horror 101 you need dark scenes, scared characters, a weak protagonist for the audience to empathize to face the 'beast' and a slimy, formless, sublime creature with tentacles, limbs, sharp teeth, spits...etc. All these elements are really well done with the original Alien in 1979 without having a potential technological counterpart. That's why it's a masterpiece! But for Prometheus the problems appear mostly due to the rushed and forced aspects of the plot and the textbook application of some fundamental concepts for alien designs.

Although the first half of the film is phenomenal with good visuals, introduction of characters, explanation of relationships and mission, there are still some glitches - like the infertility of Shaw, rushing of the expedition, exposure of David's secret agenda...etc. In the second half we understand that the crew is dispensable as they are meant to fall like domino so that we can face the final scene between Shaw and Engineer as planned. The main problem here is the rushed fact of how these characters die. In Alien(1979) for every death there was rising tension that builds up a momentum for a tragedy to happen. It was also the carrying element of the film towards the final showdown. But with Prometheus the deaths are quite instant that makes the plot 'work', the film flow and us get bombarded with action. It was a similar characteristic of the new Star Trek film as well that shows a commercial intention rather than artistic film-making.

There are also other biological problems with the film that forces some concepts to be destroyed and reinvented as pure fiction. It is possible to imagine a super fluid that causes high rate mutation, but biologically it's impossible for a human to breed a 'squid' with an umbilical cord naturally. The genius behind the Alien was the resemblance of a parasite to the host. This was present in Alien (bipedal) and Alien 3 (quadrupedal). It seems like the writers needed a 'scary' monster and picked Shaw as the victim to face this fictional part of the story. Another problem is the new 'face-hugger' that resembles a snake with little fans that covers its mouth. If it's a parasite to inter-penetrate a host through an opening, it would need supplementary organs to help it. Again comparing it to the original Alien, where the design of face-hugger was bi-symmetrical and it had limbs and tails that looked like a horseshoe crab without a shell. And it used all those elements to achieve a certain goal to lay down the egg. It it were to be a snake, it wouldn't enter another biological form, but rather ingest it because its form is expandable. We can see the contrast via comparing the larger monster in the film to the smaller one, as the larger one battles the last engineers it wins the battle with its long tentacles that helps it to get closer to its victim.

The secret behind waking Mr.Weyland is to get answers to his search for 'immortality' not to understand why human beings are created. Aside from Hayflick limit in cells, there needs to be a cycle and dynamism of death and life. Old cells need to be replaced by new. Thus, life has an irreversible fact of becoming. If it were static, things wouldn't be able to grow or transform - taking away all the vitality of it. In terms of evolution life is believed to head towards perfection or a god-like entity. Then the matching of the Dna with engineers is a spot on remark. But this still does not explain the hostile nature of an advanced alien species. Nature does not operate through destruction (The reference to Darwinism is a mistake, I am sure biology will take a different route in 21 century), but through pure creation or productivity. It would have been better to show the seed of life as a source of creativity like the film Fountain, rather than destruction of it via sacrifice of suicide. But this is not the intention of the film. It needs to be of horror, of destruction, and of fictional elements that fail to scare the audience and hypnotize them with advanced CGI.

title: A quasi-prequel that delivers nice FX but corrupts the Alien canon
review: I know many have already stated this, but here goes: the film looks great, but the pseudo-philosophy and ersatz science of the story and premise are pretty weak. And why must every space faring crew include unlikable morons and goof-balls with anger-management issues? These are supposed to be top-notch scientists and some behave like horny juveniles and cyber-punks on meth. The characters are stereotypes and clichés. Having said that, the links to the original Alien universe are welcome after the lousy AVP series muddied things up. The set design and H.R. Giger motifs are beautifully rendered. But again, the script has serious problems in logic. Why must an advanced race of space travellers sacrifice themselves to "seed" a planet with DNA? We in the 21st century are able to extract organic material without killing ourselves - why can't they? If the Engineers' DNA is a "perfect identical match" with our own, after millions of years of evolution, why aren't we 10-foot-tall white-skinned humanoids with big black eyes like them? It'd be more plausible if the match were 99% instead. The Engineer/Space Jockey who's revived erupts into a homicidal rampage for no apparent reason. Pretty primitive behavior for an intelligent, enlightened being who supposedly fathered our species. I just wish somebody with more knowledge in science, biology and human behavior had worked on the script before Ridley Scott was given $150,000,000 to spend on this ambitious, but seriously flawed production. It could have been a worthy entry in the franchise instead of a half-baked hodge-podge mess.

title: Philosophical, subtle and scary
review: First, let me state that I love some of the elements of all of the first three Alien-films: the promise of fright rather than the plastic monster has always been much scarier to me. Second, I like the idea of incorporating something more to a scary film than just sneak-sneak-THERE'S-THE-MONSTER!!. So, "Prometheus" actually does a fine job at this. It's subtly directed, letting the characters and the actors speak for themselves. The sound and cinematography definitely helps, apart from choosing brilliant actors like Michael Fassbender, Guy Pearce, Charlize Theron and Sean Harris. This film is scary, mostly in a philosophical way, for me questioning humanity, our right to life and our seemingly God-given right to be the top of the food chain; this film probably gives the best slant of the latter for a film than any I've seen in ages. On a stream of consciousness-tip, I can't really state how much the image of an alien that first looks like a penis and then transforms into a vagina-flower-with-penile-stem has haunted me. Recommendable.

title: Insight to the future....
review:
1) We still cannot think to go left or right when a wheel of a spaceship is barreling towards us resulting in death.

2) We are scared out of our pants, get lost, but still feel compelled that we should get up in the face of something that resembles an alien snake. It hisses, so that means it wants me to pet it.

3) Women's pain threshold rises. We can have a C-Section, get up to run, take a jab to the abdomen from a gun and jump about 6 feet crashing into the "wall" with our abdomen taking the brunt.

4) Going without sex for 2 yrs makes us forward; you want to get laid.

5) Weapon of choice is and always will be...the flame thrower.

....overall, Aliens always rock.

title: An Entertaining Movie With A Weak Connecting Plot
review:
I am going to keep this brief, and I want to start off by saying that I am not a die-hard fan of the series. However, I have always thought of the first two aliens as one of the most innovating, fun series for it's genre.

This movie was, at the end of the day, a let down for me. You mean to tell me, Mr. Scott, that the aliens indirectly spawned from humans? The same alien that was supposed to be the perfect specimen that had acid for blood? I get some of the ways the alien ultimately popped out of about 3 or 4 different species intertwining their respective character traits, but such a perfect specimen as the alien was always presented to be felt that there should have been a sense of mystery and not a direct result of different species combining (including HUMANS). It was just a let down for me. I cannot believe that the alien that has had such a dramatic effect on cinematic history would not have spawned had it not been for human intervention. That is just a let down for me. I do not know what everyone else felt, but that plot detail upset me. I loved the movie otherwise, but whenever I go back and watch the originals, I am going to try and block out this movie's plot.

title: A mixed bag
review:
The movie starts of pretty well. We are brought into the world of the film with breathtaking visuals. All throughout the movie a lot of questions are raised that keeps you guessing what is going to be revealed in the end. There is somewhat of a tension that keeps building up for an awesome climax that unfortunately never was.

There are a lot of subplots and even the main plot that is never brought to their satisfying end. The characters behave erratically at times and even completely opposite to the way that they have behaved previously. There is hardly any character development for a lot of cast you don't feel anything for them even when they sacrifice themselves or die.I only was interested in characters played by Noomi and Michael. Charlize was wasted and plot "twist" around her character was so obvious.

Overall pretty visuals, amazing sound, a story that puts up too many questions and answers none of them, pretty average acting. As a standalone film, it is not very very good but still worth a one time watch. The other parts of this trilogy should answer some of the questions left unanswered in this. In the end this only felt like a filler for something better coming. Go watch if you are a sci fi buff who wants more from the "Alien" universe.

title: Prometheus' journey parallels 2001:A Space Odyssey
review:
I can definitely say the movie needs 2 viewings. Was it too long, slow and boring at times, yes, but worth seeing anyway; especially on the big screen. Now, right off, I must say I am not a fan of the Alien movies; However, 2001:A Space a Odyssey plot and story line parallel this movie.

The Space Jockeys (SJs) were creators of life on Earth, and perhaps on many other worlds as well. They guided humanity, as is evidenced by the cave drawings depicting aliens pointing towards their world. However, as is pointed out in the movie, this goes against Darwinian evolution. Perhaps, it's a different universe in which human evolution and history took a different path.

Cave drawings point to a solar system; However, as we learn in the film, the planet is actually a military base stocked with bio-weapons. Thus, logically, why would aliens invite humans to travel to an (apparently not so secret) military base, or even reveal its location for that matter? Ifcourse, 35k years ago, the planet might have been lived on, but by the time of the events in the film, it is not any longer.

My theory however, is these drawings were not invitations to visit the SJs; this whole thing was a setup. If eventually the creation(humans) become intelligent enough to be able to seek out the creator and travel to the stars, humanity(and any other intelligent species) are destroyed. The SJ's could not allow, or were afraid, of other life forms reaching out that far, reaching the gods, becoming as intelligent, or even killing the SJs and taking over.

Adam&Eve eating from the tree of knowledge, and being cast out; in 2001, HAL killing the humans for fear of itself being shut off; Terminator's Skynet nuking humans as they try to disconnect(kill) it when it becomes "self-aware", attaining human-level intelligence and/or regards itself as alive, etc.; Dr.Frankenstein's monster, the Golem, Westworld, Colossus: The Forbin Project, Event Horizon, etc. Star Trek the MP's V'Ger seeks its creator, and will kill unless the creator responds. In Blade Runner, replicants are hunted down; again, creator destroying his (superior) creation out of fear of it.

At some point, the SJs did plan to wipe out humans by using those bio weapons, but... they were stopped by those who created _them_. For, you see, even the SJs have a creator. The higher gods probably realized the SJs creation is now greater or above them.

Ifcourse, if the SJs really did want humans to travel to their world, then they could have left a more advanced item, or sentinel, or probe, on Earth or on the Moon, instead of forcing humans to go by 35,000 year old cave paintings. Not much to go on, except faith, that the paintings are right. A machine, which when activated, reveals the whole back story to humans.

Which is why the monolith in 2001 which was found on the moon sends a signal to Jupiter announcing man's arrival, meaning humans have attained a level of tech capable of space travel... now, they have to prove themselves greater than their creations: tools, machines, computers.

Humans' ultimate creation, a talking thinking computer that has attained conscience, it is self-aware, and regards itself as alive. It fights to stay alive, as all living things do. Once man defeats the machine(his creation), he is transformed into a higher being/life form.

2001 had the better idea of aliens leaving a monolith on the moon. Only advanced enough beings could fly to other bodies in the solar system; Likewise, had 15th c. Europeans wanted the Indians to travel across the ocean to Europe, they would have transmitted knowledge as to how to build ships, and navigation charts, and other necessary info. From the film I deduce that at some point the aliens did leave Earth thousands of years ago. For if they hadn't, there would've been other evidence of SJs visits besides cave paintings, and then knowledge of the SJs existence would have been known to the scientists in the present.

Thus, the space journey parallels that of 2001's; a trip into the unknown based on an alien artifact. In fact, the opening shots in both movies are practically the same. However, the aliens of 2001 did not create life on Earth; they just implant intelligence into a species capable of evolving.

As for how the alien at the end fits into all this, or why the black goo turns people into zombies, I do not know.

Does the fact the movie takes place at Christmas, and an event that took place 2000 years ago, and a woman incapable of bearing children does give birth, proves the movie is a Christian motif?

Was the planned destruction of humanity in revenge for killing an alien messenger(Jesus)? Possible. But, how could primitives capture and crucify an alien? And even if so, what's the connection to the SJ's planet, and all but 1 being killed? Also, why should all humanity on planet Earth be killed for actions of a few Romans or Jews or whomever it was that crucified Jesus/alien?

Does, perhaps the ultimate God stop the SJs from killing an entire species because of actions of a few in Palestine? Perhaps. But I still say the entire cave drawings, come to us message was a Trojan horse; a barrier of intelligence which once crossed sets off an alarm, and a plan to destroy humans by leading them into a death trap.

Ultimately, the point is an intelligent creation must die, for it will learn with no bounds, and eventually kill the creator. As opposed to 2001's point, which is that intelligence is rewarded; at the end man is on his 1st steps, transformed into the star child.

title: It's no ALIEN!
review: Alien was a unique film. Unlike today's sci-fi blockbusters which rely on computer-generated effects, loud eyeball-blasting, eardrum-splitting explosions, Alien took a different approach. What made Alien work so well was QUIET, SIMPLE TERROR. Special effects were kept to a minimum. Not one gun was fired. Mood, plot, and character development were everything. The storyline was SIMPLE...The crew goes out to investigate a signal. They unknowingly bring back an alien life form which proceeds to kill off crew members one by one. That's it. SIMPLE! We, the audience, sat and witnessed the TERROR build with QUIET intensity in Ridley Scott's masterpiece, which, in my estimation, will always be the perfect film. Unfortunately, there will never be another like it. Switch to Prometheus, which is everything Alien wasn't. I really wanted to like Prometheus and I entered the theater with every expectation that I would love it. After all it was Ridley Scott. However the plot was so incredibly convoluted I started to get bored. From the outset, I was confused. Who was the alien? What did he drink? Why? What happened to him? Why? What did that scene have to do with anything? When a movie starts off with a bunch of unanswered questions and continues on that path, it's usually a bad sign. It was. I sat there watching scene after disconnected scene as my disappointment grew. Disappointment - not terror or suspense. Where was the intensity? There was none! Not even twelve hours have passed since I saw Prometheus, and, in my mind, it is already a forgotten film. Too bad Ridley. I expected so much more.

title: Exhilarating, Exciting, and Enjoyable. However...
review:
I went into the cinema with limited expectations, having never seen the Alien films. Although I knew all about the Alien mythos and the details of its universe, I never actually saw the movies. Yes, I know, what a life. But really, this fact made it much easier for me to like this film mainly because Prometheus answered whatever questions I had regarding Alien (at least, surface questions I formed based on assumptions and general understandings), and posed other interesting questions in addition--questions that blockbuster movies don't usually pose. Therefore I wasn't bothered much by the whole "doesn't answer all the questions only gives more questions" thing because I had never seen the Alien movies to begin with.

I am a big Sci Fi fan, from books to movies to the idea. And this movie, visually and ideally, fulfilled all my fantastical Sci Fi expectations. I was hooked, completely intrigued and stunned from the opening scene. Despite the build-up being intentionally dawning, it worked for me. Every new scene that popped up pleased me. If it didn't please me, it freaked the hell out of me, especially the birthing scene in the medpod.

Of course, gradually the exhilaration started to die out as the scientists committed some really avoidable mistakes and did some really unnecessary things just to get the plot moving, but all that didn't really affect me as I was more immersed in the whole environment and situation that they found themselves in. I didn't care that they did completely retarded things, because the result was always completely gratifying.

So here's my breakdown: 1) Opening scene is breathtaking and intriguing, although this kind of landscape eagle eye view thing has been attempted many times before. 2) I wish they would've had some more sets to work with, instead of just the Engineer's tomb/ship and the Prometheus. However I understand that this wouldn't fit with the storyline, the planet being simply a military outpost and all. 3) Michael Fassbender was fantastic as David--a real highlight of the movie. This simple character can easily meld in and out of plot lines and adds more intrigue to the entire movie, being a half-robot. 4) The scene before and when David wakes the passengers has this easy breezy Wall-E-esque feel to it, adding more to the nostalgic Sci Fi vibe.

In the end, even though Prometheus leaves more questions at its conclusion, it didn't bother me much because I was there all for the visual spectacle and unabashed harking to the glorious days of Sci Fi. The enjoyable performances from Fassbender, Theron and Rapace helped too. I don't watch movies for questions to be answered about previous movies, I watch them for the ride, and Prometheus sure brought me on a ride I won't soon forget. I highly recommend this movie for people looking to cringe in their seats and get thrilled.

title: Mankind's Search for Truth and Meaning
review:
Fundamentally, Ridley Scott's "Prometheus" is about the search for truth and meaning. Under the guise of a 3D science fiction thriller, it begs most of humanity's most basic spiritual and/or philosophical questions. Why are we here? Were we created, and if so, by who or what? Is there a purpose to our very being? The film does not presume to answer all of the above, although it does leave us with the strong possibility that such truths are not only out there but can be found. It's no coincidence that the film's title is also the name of the immortal Greek titan that sculpted mankind into existence from clay. He also enabled mankind's progress by giving them the fire he stole from the gods; he championed us to such an extent that he would ultimately be punished for it, condemned by Zeus to endure an eternity of having his liver pecked out by an eagle.

Most potential audiences cannot be expected to see this film from a more introspective angle. It will be regarded primarily as the semi-prequel to Scott's own 1979 film "Alien," a great horror film in its own right but obviously devoid of any spiritual subtexts. Keen observers should be able to spot all of the references, from the overt inclusions of the "space jockey" and the crescent-shaped alien spacecraft to the subtler throwbacks in characterization, production design, and tone. I personally pride myself on having caught an instance in which a section of music from Jerry Goldsmith's "Alien" score was mixed into the soundtrack. Those seeking any obvious inclusion of the now well-known alien creatures are likely to be disappointed, not because the film lacks close encounters with extraterrestrials but because they introduce themselves through a deliberate and somewhat confusing process of evolution.

The story proper begins in the year 2089 when, on an archaeological expedition on an isle off the coast of Scotland, scientist couple Elizabeth Shaw (Noomi Rapace) and Charlie Holloway (Logan Marshall-Green) discover a cave with a painting of a star map. This is but one of many star maps found around the world, which is unusual given the fact that the sites on which they were found belonged to ancient cultures separated by time and distance. Shaw, without a doubt a believer in a higher power, interprets these findings as an invitation from humanity's outer space forerunners, dubbed the Engineers. Quite simply, it's a chance to learn who we are and where we came from. Four years later, a privately funded interstellar expedition aboard the starship "Prometheus" arrives at the only logical location outlined in the star maps: A moon in a very distant part of the galaxy.

The crew consists of your usual grab-bag of mechanical and scientific experts, including Shaw and Holloway. Of particular interest are two characters. One is David (Michael Fassbender), an android; while initially no more than a machine, unclouded by emotions or morality, his mechanically superior ability to process and learn gradually gives him something of a superiority complex towards the human passengers. The other is Meredith Vickers (Charlize Theron). She has been sent by the company funding the expedition, the Weyland Corporation, to monitor the crew. Level-headed yet elusive and controlling, we spend most of the film trying to determine what her hidden agenda is. Perhaps it has something to do with a holographic projection of the company's long-gone founder, the deeply wizened Peter Weyland (Guy Pearce).

After landing on the moon, Shaw and her team soon uncover a sprawling network of underground caves and corridors, which inexplicably produce an atmosphere capable of sustaining human life. Their expedition reveals the remains of an Engineer's head, along with a vast subterranean cavern well-stocked with cylinder-like urns. Upon their discovery, the urns begin to leak a strange black goo. David is the first to discover this. As he secretly stashes an urn on the ship and conducts an experiment, Shaw is thrilled to learn that the Engineers' DNA is identical to a human's. But then begins a biological epidemic begins to infect the crew; it reaches such a degree that Shaw is forced to conclude that she was wrong about the Engineers' intentions.

The original "Alien" achieved a shocking visceral thrill with the infamous chestburster sequence, a turn of events that audiences at that time could not have foreseen. "Prometheus" attempts to outdo its predecessor with its own disturbing birth scene, one that kick starts an unstoppable evolutionary process. As to whether or not it's successful, that's entirely a matter of personal opinion. I admittedly had a difficult time navigating the story's biological path of destruction, as I found the link between organism and host convoluted. My response to the less tangible spiritual aspects was much better. "Prometheus" is at its best when it speculates on the unknown. Like Shaw, many of us have chosen to believe in something greater than ourselves. Unlike Shaw, we tend to leave it at that. She's not content with mere blind faith. She will always be searching.

-- Chris Pandolfi (www.atatheaternearyou.net)

title: Overlooked Classic
review: Most reviews that i have read about this movie are just complaining about how unrealistic this movie is, how lame the plot is, and how many cheezy lines there are....has everyone failed to realise that this is a SCI FI MOVIE!! has anyone even seen the first alien????? There were plenty of cheezy lines and unrealistic parts. thats just ridleys style, do other great sci fi movies like independence day, the thing, terminator, and the predator all have scripts that go deep into scientific reasons for everything. The entertainment value for this movie was 10/10 keeping u on the edge of your seat, with beautiful flawless visuals, and many memorable moments, full of burning flesh and corroding faces. Although it has kind of a slow beginning it seems to build up anticipation for when the action comes similar to the beginning of The Descent. Although it was a simple plot, it had tons of twists and turns that kept it feeling fresh. AWESOME!!! 9/10

title: Can I have my Sick Squid back?
review: I kind of expected this movie to be a let down and lowered my expectations accordingly. Sadly not low enough. The cinematography is breathtaking and the cast are top drawer, especially Fassbender, who demonstrates why he is probably the finest actor working in movies today. The fatal flaw in this movie though is the second rate writing, which is so amateurish it feels like it was conceived by a couple of 13 year old schoolboys after an all night Syfy channel marathon. The illogical actions of some of the characters are well documented in other reviews here and in my opinion this is what ruins the movie (i.e. performing a DIY caesarean section on yourself, stapling up the gash then running around 5 mins later like Ellen Ripley on Red Bull). Ridley Scott is known to be a perfectionist, so why he agreed to shoot with such a shoddy script and story is a mystery. Also, whoever gave the green light to the design of the 'aliens' needs to be put into hypersleep for a very long time. They are truly laughable. On the one hand you have the 'Engineers', who are super intelligent pseudo gods, but who resemble a Right Said Fred tribute act and behave like Vinnie Jones on a bad day. I suppose everyone gets a bit grouchy if they are awakened out of a deep sleep by a bunch of strangers poking around in your crib. . . . Then there are the Flesh Gordon style 'cock-cobras' and don't even get me started on the alien squid that is so B Movie it would make Charles Band Blush. Surely we are beyond slimy tentacled aliens by now? The film lacks the suspense, intelligence and cohesion of Alien and I suspect that all the pre-release efforts to distance them from each other was due to the acknowledgement that it was not in the same league as the original and could never compare. Worth seeing for Fassbender alone, but other than that another damp squid, sorry squib, in the franchise.

title: Crappy, big disappointment, boring
review:
These are the words to describe Prometheus. It was in fact a crappy movie compared to the best in 2012. I will give it a 6/10 here, only of the goodness of my heart and for some cool effects. But the story was a old story in new wrapping...or was it old story in old wrapping. I do not know. I caught myself almost falling a sleep in the middle of this boring movie. This movie is blown up to be a "WOW!" Must see movie..but no...waste of money, I urge people to don't go to the cinema for this it isn't worth it. To make a point to this worse ever Ridley Scott movie, just download it when it comes on any torrent, because it really ain't worth the penny to see. I used $30 on a 3D viewing of this movie, and are very disappointed.

Ridley Scott you know you can do better than that!

title: Ridley Scott's masterfarce
review:
What a heartbreak for a die-hard Ridley Scott fan. One can only wonder how the same director who made Gladiator, Kingdom of Heaven, A Good Year, Black Hawk Down would pick up a script as childish as this. It's a thriller that doesn't thrill and is totally devoid of sensibility. It should suffice to say that the most thrilling moments of the movie came halfway through it when the first deaths occur. The rest just petered out like damp fireworks.

Charlize Theron must surely be running out of money to be shooting stuff like this. Noomi Rapace tries but the script doesn't let her. Fassbender will do well to avoid such movies in the future.

We have come to expect a lot from Mr Scott in recent years and with this movie he has picked those expectations up and absolutely ripped them to pieces. I consider Alien to be an OK movie, yet considering that it was made in 1979 it was quite an achievement. And elements such as Ash the cold-blooded android were pleasantly amazing. But the man has not made a sci-fi flick in years and it shows. This is 2012 and just VFX and the label 'science-fiction' do not work anymore.

I would give it a 4/10 but the visuals make it a 5.

And whoever can explain to me the connection between the end of the first scene and the rest of the movie shall get a 100 bucks wired to his account. Or how the Space Jockey from Alien dies inside the human spacecraft in this movie. Or how a woman who has just had a major surgery, hits the ground running the very next moment, literally.

title: Movie fails
review:
********** S P O I L E R **********

I just came home from the movie theater where i saw Prometheus. Overall it was a good movie with a few awesome 3D effects. But i still left the movie theater with a feeling of frustration because of the ending. The whole foundation of the movie was that these Engineers supposedly created mankind, but now we found out that they had started creating weapons of mass destruction and planned an attack against earth. A good story in itself. The frustrating part was that we never got to find out what was behind this decision to destroy earth. Why were the Engineers so disappointed with their human creation that it drove them to wanting to obliterate the entire species of mankind? Where did the writers of the movie hide the back-story for this? Sure, it's up to each viewer to interpret this, but i want the view from the creators of the movie, what did they have in mind by letting this movie go the way it did?

I'm comparing the ending of this movie with how it would have looked like if "Lord Of The Rings: Return Of The King" had ended with Frodo standing on the edge with the ring, without letting us know whether he threw it in the flames or not. This isn't what we want, we wanna see that he threw the ring into the flames. And i wanna know the background story as to why human kind as a creation had to be eliminated. Not based on everyone's own theories, but by the creators of this movie showing us. That's why Prometheus feels like a fail in my opinion, a good movie that is ruined by a bad ending.

If they're planning a Prometheus 2, perhaps as a prequel where we get to see the Engineers planning and their motive for why human kind should be eliminated, then i can accept this movie as a nice piece of work. But if it ends like this, it's just a fail.

title: Ridley Scott, where have you disappeared to?
review:
Let me start off by saying I have never seen any of the 1970's Alien movies. Therefore, I will not be comparing Prometheus to Scott's apparent 70's "gold". Regardless, I have seen Gladiator, American Gangster, and Robin Hood as of late, the first one mentioned being the best of the three. Hard to argue with that.

Having said that, Robin Hood was awful. This is going to seem like unintelligible discourse but that movie was absolute horse dung. The most boring movie I have seen to date and it cannot even hold a candle close to the 1991 Robin Hood starring Kevin Costner. So needless to say I wasn't expecting much from Ridley Scott's 2012 sci-fi flick.

Prometheus is a futuristic 2093 space science fiction epic film with the basic plot line that contains something along the lines of humans going out to find the beginning to their proverbial existence. This inevitably brings out the taboo topic of evolution vs. creationism but alas, the topic, which has so many possibilities, peaks and valleys, is thrown by the wayside and a much more haphazard design is espoused: one that cannot even be described in words because I honestly do not know what happened.

To explain, there were many instances in the movie where I just sat back and had to say "What?". Shaw gets an emergency c section and subsequently has her stomach stapled shut, but the crew of the vessel hardly pays attention to her. The woman just got emergency surgery yet it is completely dumped from the plot, as if her being pregnant was as common an occurrence as the Patriots making the playoffs. I understand that no one else knew about the happening but the fact that the writer simply waved it off as a minor token in a seemingly bulletproof story line was extremely confusing. There is also the fact that Shaw can run, jump, crawl and play Jenga when she just underwent major surgery, but I will ignore this point due to the fact that she's tweaked up a bunch of drugs during- and post-operation - drugs that are probably futuristic and do a barrage of different things.

When the two scientists get lost near the beginning of the story (the biologist and the geologist), they find a cave with a bunch of alien "vase"-looking pustules. When a completely undiscovered and unknown life form pokes its "head" from the murky depths of the galactic tar, these two geniuses think that it's a good idea to touch it. Needless to say they both die, although the geologist has one more sprite-ly encounter before meeting his doom in the form of APC tires and flamethrower fuel. This movie could have been so much more than 45 minutes of build-up to barely disgusting/spooky horror scenes and an ending that just screams "Sequel". It could have made us wonder about the philosophical journey that the human race made from the expanse of history or had us question whether God does exist. Even a story that had absolutely no thesis besides the "aliens are here, let's look around" synopsis would have been better, when compared to the way were teased with a deeper plot and never got the satisfaction we were craving for.

The good news is this movie revolutionized the way CGI is used in movies today. I would go as far as to say this movie is almost on par with Avatar in it's visual prowess and special effects. The alien planet looks marvelous and the make-up the artists use for the actors/actresses is astounding in quality. This is one visually appealing film that is worth owning on Blu-ray, if only for the eye candy. And alas, Michael Fassbender, you have again saved the show. Being the proverbial gold nugget in a river of dull rocks and Charlize Theron, his portrayal of the android David seals the deal for me as the best acting performance in the entire movie, and one of the best displays in Fassbender's career. Even in extreme situations his soft voice and calm demeanor makes us think that everything is okay - he even makes us chuckle at times, when making a quip about Shaw's vivid surgery (which once again shows that his movie did not take it seriously).

All-in-all, Prometheus provides a stunning display of visual effects and Fassbender's performance almost saves this film for me - almost. If it were not for the completely random plot, lack of character development, and seeming lack of concern for the viewers intelligence, this movie would have gotten a 6, maybe a 7. For now it stays at a 5, until the Director's Cut (crossing my fingers) comes out and fills in some of the plot holes it left.

title: A shadow of his former self
review:
Mr Ridley Scott has made a new film: Prometheus - a Science Fiction movie

The title is promising: Prometheus is a figure from the Greek Mythology, the creator of the human race. Considering that Ridley Scott made some great films (Blade runner, Alien, Thelma and Louise) I was looking forward to seeing this one.

What a disappointment! After a promising start and an impressive visual introduction à la Space Odyssey (interesting: Michael Fassbender) the movie gets more and more stereotype and predictable. The whole plot along with some scenes reminded me strongly of Alien. It seemed that Mr. Scott was counting on gaining new fans who didn't see Alien more than he was afraid of his old fans uncovering his lack of talent and originality.

For someone who knew Scott's former movies, this was bound to be a disappointment: Nothing new, nothing interesting, nothing that had a real connection with the myth of Prometheus, not once suspenseful. Instead: brainless entertainment packed with special effects - not badly done - but soulless like all today's blockbusters, boring and without any real reason of existence. A pale copy of his old movie idea in Alien.

At the end, as was somehow suspected, the first Alien monster is born and it's clear that Prometheus was meant to be a prequel to Alien (how it all began) But all in all it made no sense at all.

1 point for Mr. Fassbender

1 point for Noomi Rapace

1 point for the promising first 15 minutes.

The rest is not worth mentioning

title: So why is Prometheus a dull film?
review:
So why is Prometheus a dull film? There's obviously a lot of money sloshing around; the direction is okay and the SFX is okay. What went wrong? The major, glaring flaw is the script and dialogue. To quote the great Bart Simpson, "I didn't think it was physically possible, but this both sucks and blows."

SPOILERS AHEAD: The first Alien film is rightly a sci-fi masterpiece. One area where Alien clearly excels over Prometheus is in the crew interaction. Prometheus is a very similar film (in fact it's actually a remake: aliens, far away, android crew member is evil etc etc); the crew are on a spaceship (more or less) and stuff goes wrong, people die, aliens cruise around etc etc. Except that in Prometheus the people are artificial (and I don't mean the android); there's no realistic interaction between any of the crew. They don't talk to each other at all about what is going on. Some of them die, and there's NO conversation. Not even a tense _lack_ of conversation. Some of the crew are trapped in the alien base, and no one cares that they were left behind (except the poor trapped guys obviously). Charlize Theron burns one of the crew alive and there's NO mention of it afterwards. I cannot stress this enough. It is a fault so massive that I can only assume that Ridley Scott and the other people involved were deaf, since that's the only way you'd miss it. It's artificial and fake, and it sucks the heart right out of the film. Whoever wrote the dialogue ought to be ashamed of themselves and quit screen writing.

There's also very, very few scary moments (the R rating appears to come completely from a single scene, which is also rather dull except for the squirm factor). Instead, the writers have decided that awe-inspiring alien vistas and star-map holograms are more important. What this functionally translates into is a lack of tension in the entire film. That's Ridley Scott's fault, and it's obvious that he's lost his touch here.

Overall, it's dull, lifeless, and empty. Which is a shame because the ingredients are all there. It's just that the chef can't read the recipe correctly. 5 out of 10. Catch it on DVD. It's not worth cinema prices.

title: Great film, if you don't think about it too much.
review:
I'll start with the good stuff. Design, visual effects sound and mood are amazing. Shooting on location did add a sense of scale to the long landscape shots which is harder to achieve with a matte-painting.

Michael Fassbender is amazing as David. His character is brilliantly acted, strangely motivated and enchanting. Definitely the most memorable character in this movie.

But aside from the fact that this was an enjoyable film, when I walked away I began thinking about what I had just watched, certain points came back into my mind which didn't sit right.

The biggest gripe I had with the film was the lack of development of incredible ideas. While watching the movie I thought they'd come back later on, but they didn't.

Spoilers -

Firstly, David could watch the dreams of the sleeping people. This could have been an excellent plot device, but it was only mentioned 3 times. I was sure they were going to use it to have David communicate directly with the sleeping Engineers.

Secondly, after the beautifully paced intro, everything happened too fast. All of a sudden they were at the planet (moon?), everyone was awake, they landed, they were inside, they saw the holographic aliens, David decoded the alien language and opened a door. It just all happened so quickly, there was no point at which they were really exploring the unknown.

It felt like the film was trying too hard to be an action movie, a sci-fi movie and a horror film. I found there to be a lack of suspense, and nothing hiding in the dark. Everything was so conveniently well lit. This may be the fault of being shot for 3d.

Then there were the plot holes; 1) This race of engineers had visited humanity first to mix their DNA with the primordial ooze. Then they came back to earth several times to show some of Earths earliest civilization's where, exactly, in space their top secret military bases were located. And apparently "invited" us to come visit.

2) The plot reveals were too obvious. If this had been a straight-out action movie, then I wouldn't have a problem with this. But Ridley Scott was attempting to tackle some heavy intellectual/religious issues. And if you're going to make a Movie like that then you would make your twists less obvious and more epic. The fact that Weyland was on the ship too obvious, and they foreshadowed it multiple times before revealing it. The pause before Charlize said "...father" was almost painful. I don't see how the mission would have changed much if Charlize had just said from the offset that the mission was funded by her father and he was on a quest for the holy grail. That wouldn't have affected the work that the scientists were doing at all.

3) The scientists were all stupid! No-one was following any sort of safety requirements or quarantine procedures. Dr Holloway taking his helmet off to test the air, yeah, I can believe that with his character. But the others only waited 5-seconds before removing their own helmets. None of them put their helmets back on AFTER seeing their first dead alien and opening a hermetically sealed chamber. They didn't know what diseases the alien was carrying. The botanist should have known better. But then, he was busy getting lost with the only guy who should have not been able to get lost. The geologist Fitfield. He had the laser mapping "Pups". He shouldn't have gotten lost! Milburn and Fitfield are idiots. They ran away from the decapitated Engineer, and the "Lifeform" detected by the pup, but when they see a completely unknown alien snake, Milburn attempts to pet it? As with most of the deaths in this film, it just made me think. "Well, to be honest, he did deserve that"

4) Why did the Engineer chase Elizabeth to try and kill her? And how did he get to her? They breathe the same air we do. So how did he make it to her ship without his spacesuit?

5) Confusing alien life-cycle - Too many steps: David smuggles the canister back to the ship and slips a bit of "alien" into Dr Holloway's drink. He is infected with the stuff that made the Engineers head explode. So then he has sex with Elizabeth and impregnated her with the next stage of the alien. There was very little time between the initial infection and the point at which his head was going to explode, and in this time the alien life-cycle depended on him having intercourse to pass on the bug. So, then the baby squid starts to gestate within Elizabeth, it grows really fast and she removes it, but essentially is a giant Facehugger. Which then ends up getting the Engineer and impregnates him, which then turns into a traditional Xenomorph - almost recognizable from the original movie (but probably different due to DNA differences in the Engineer.

Then we have the alien that attacks Fitfield and Milburn. They both get attacked by the same "Snakes". However, one is turned into a killer zombie and one was killed outright.

6) The film makers went to a lot of effort to recreate some of the major set pieces from the original Alien, however they were on the wrong planet. The amazing space ship crashing scene, which managed to land in effectively the same way as they found the ship in Alien, as well as a distress/warning signal and the Engineer's massive space telescope were all there. And yet it means nothing because it was not the same planet which the Nostromo lands on in Alien, 29 years later.

To sum up my feeling about this movie, I thought it was great. But I came in expecting a more intellectual and challenging film.

title: Prometheus : a fair review
review:
This is a Sci-Fi movie. There's no better way of putting it. Forget about people calling it a Sci-Fi horror or a Sci-Fi monster flick, although it being, sort of, a prequel to the Alien quadrilogy. It's a Sci-Fi movie. Full Stop.

With that in mind I watched Prometheus yesterday. I was disappointed that my friend bought 3D tickets, since I'm just not a big fan of 3D. But apparently it only ran in 3D. That said one of the first things that came to my attention were the beautiful sceneries and consistent 3D shots. The entire movie looks breathtaking. Stunning visuals.

Secondly I witnessed really good acting (Noomi Rapace, Michael Fassbender, Charlize Thereon). All 3 really were very well cast. The remainder of the characters/actors however are all a bit shallow, and are given few airtime and depth.

The best part however is the plot. In true Sci-Fi fashion it dwells on the big questions in life. Or should I say question ? Where do we come from ? Driven by perfect audio and clever dialogue the story is really build up well. Prometheus also has a very consistent "alien" mood which makes it a worthy prequel.

I liked it A lot. 8 out of 10.

title: Prometheus has landed!
review:
One of the most eagerly anticipated films of the year.

I managed to get into a midnight showing of this at the O2. Not a full house, but that's mostly because of the time it was being shown at. Ridley Scott has said in many of his interviews before it's release, that he wanted to make another Alien film true to the original story. He stated how disappointed he had become with Alien franchise over the years, in particular the Alien Vs Predator movies. So he decided to make Prometheus to set the record straight.

Where do I start with Prometheus?

It's not a masterpiece, but it's a very good, very dark sci-fi film, as well as the best film I've seen in 3D to date. I highly recommend an IMAX viewing of this. The film makes amazing use of 3D and an IMAX screening would only enhance the viewing experience for cinema goers.

The performances are excellent. Cannot fault any one of the actors for the roles they played. Of course, there are always standouts. By standouts I mean, Noomi Rapace as Elizabeth Shaw and the brilliant Michael Fassbender as the android David. Both are absolutely fantastic in this. Rapace is every much the heroine and in this film. Not only does she own the character, but I almost forgot that she's the actress playing a character. Her character goes through so much physical and emotional pain in this film, it's amazing how she manages to survive it all. One scene in particular (bit of a spoiler) involving Shaw, an operating table and an alien baby being delivered by caesarean, will be very hard to forget after you see it. She matches Ripley in intellect, emotion and strength. Whether or not they'll be a sequel about her character remains to be seen.

Fassbender is brilliant as David. I'm a massive fan of this guy. And everything I've seen him do has been excellent. David works directly for Weyland Industries but is aboard Prometheus to help and assist the scientists with their research. Fassbender has massive screen presence. He's engaging, funny and utterly convincing as David the android. David like the scientists is looking for his own answers. He asks questions his own existence, why he was made and questions the nature of humanity. He models himself on Peter O'Toole's Lawrence of Arabia and quotes lines from the film. His mannerisms and speech are everything that resemble Ian Holm's Ash from the first Alien. Terrific supporting cast, Idris Elba, Charlize Theron, Guy Pearce, all do a wonderful job. Idris' southern American accent is slightly wobbly but he puts in a good shift with his performance, so it wasn't much of an issue for me.

The screenplay isn't amazing, it just plods along. If anything Fassbender and Elba have all the best lines in the film. The action set pieces are also very good as are the futuristic set designs. Ridley Scott's direction is polished, has great cinematography and is visually appealing. Filmed in several countries, the landscapes look absolutely beautiful. Just like Alien, Prometheus has a lot of creepy tension and some jump out of your seat moments, but it's not perfect. The film leaves quite a few questions unanswered and towards the end, the film felt rushed and bordered on the ridiculous. The cameo at the end is a lot to be desired and I rather they not make this inclusion to satisfy the fan boys.

If I'm being honest it should've been longer just to explain a few things that were left unexplained. The end suggest that there'll be a sequel, but I don't think Prometheus will get one, because it will go against everything Ridley Scott said he was trying to achieve.

All in all it's a good film but mostly for its performances and set pieces. The plot is daft and the story needed a lot more work, but it's a good film and I was entertained. But please, by all means see this in 3D. It's absolutely worth it.
